reviews.text: Excellent service from start to finish. He arrived on time, efficiently unclogged my kitchen sink, and left everything clean and working perfectly. Fair and reasonable pricing. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: C R
reviews.text:
Saw them out on another job. Asked for a quote. Gave me fair price, came out next morning to fix my problem.
UPDATE:::  same problem a few weeks later. Asked them to come out and address the problem. Ignored my calls for couple days then later made up & excuse to not come by & stand behind their guarantee & work. Found out from another plumber that i had to pay (half their price btw) that the clog in my drain was just pushed down the line & never cleared.

reviews.author: Carl A.
reviews.text:
The Dyna-Rooter Plumber came out to my house to replace a faucet.  He installs the faucet that I had purchased and the faucet is completely loose!  It can be turned, titled forward, back, and side-to side.  It looks and feels like it could be literally pulled out of the sink if you tried hard enough.  The plumber blamed the faucet we bought!  Even if we had purchased a bad faucet (which I don't believe to be the case - why would a manufacturer build faucets this bad?) then I should be told BEFORE installing it that there could be a problem - not after.

Also, I had two lengths of flexible tubing (one for cold, one for hot) that I had purchased at the hardware store and I left them by the new faucet box.  I was originally planning on installing it myself.  The Dyna-rooter plumber comes in, sees the tubing and faucet together and the uses my tubing, and keeps the original high cost of installation!  I paid $15 for those so I should get $15 off my bill.  He uses my equipment and charges me the same amount?  The nerve!!!   

Stay away from this made-up-named company.  Do you homework first and get reviews before having someone come do work in your home.  I learned my lesson.

reviews.author: A Horaites
reviews.text: Dyna Rooter Plumbing is absolutely fantastic!  Paul and his team are excellent at what they do. He is very honest and the quality and accuracy of the work they do is outstanding. It's hard to find honest contractors but this is my go to for any plumbing issues. They've worked on my house, my mom's house and I referred them to friends and family. Dyna Rooter Plumbing and Sewer gets the job done right the first time. I trust them completely. If you're looking for good quality, honest and affordable work to be done with any plumbing issue or remodel... call them. It's the best call you can make.

reviews.author: Mark N.
reviews.text: We had an issue that caused waste water to come up through our downstairs shower drain whenever a toilet was flushed in the house.  Paul came out to root one of the toilets and quoted us on the work that needed to be done to correct the issue.  He came out to root the toilet one more time due to an emergency prior to the scheduled work and did not charge us for that visit.  Paul was excellent and he even restored our sump pump at no additional cost during a difficult time for our family.  I couldn't recommend him and his company enough, thank you very much!!!

reviews.author: Su De
reviews.text:
Issue with outside clean-out for laundry room.   We rodded out several times to no avail.
Called Dyna Rooter.inc  (paul) and he promptly came out... he and  his worker Chris dug down and found clean-out shaft   unattached to base pipe and seal.  Roots and soil had made a home in the pipes over time.
Dug out, flushed pipes,  Re-set shaft,  resealed, cleaned and refilled hole in ample time.  Very satisfied with work  and price.
If you hv clean out shaft that rises every spring call Dyna Rooter.inc to remedy ASAP.  We didn't notice until we had a backup.

If you're looking for a plumber, shop local small business, and give Paul a call!

I have additional plumbing jobs that I already am in the process of scheduling with Paul's business, Dyna Rooter Plumbing and Sewer, Inc.

reviews.text: Twice, I’ve called upon Dyna and both times they have responded to my request very quickly and professionally.  First was to fix an outside faucet and replace another. For both of the jobs, I found his pricing to be very reasonable!!!!!!

reviews.author: Bud Goforth
reviews.text: I am very satisfied with the service and the results. Paul was able to come to my house the next day after I called him and he arrived on time. synthesis.summary: Paul consistently solves problems two or three other plumbers couldn't fix, shows up on time even on weekends and holidays, but one documented case of ignoring callback requests and pushing a clog rather than clearing it is worth knowing before you hire.

plumbers.address: 619 Estes Ave, Schaumburg, IL 60193, USA

reviews.author: Sanjay Joshi
reviews.text:
The two main water shutoff valves on either side of the water meter were about 35 years old and were not properly shutting off the water, so I called a few plumbing companies for estimates. B&A Plumbing was the most reasonable one and since their reviews were good, I decided to try this company. One company with good reviews quoted double of what B&A charged me.

Dean from B&A Plumbing came in today and I showed him the location and he quickly replaced the two valves. He then asked me to call the village to turn on the water and when they did, he checked to make sure there were no leaks before leaving. Overall, Dean was easy to work with, friendly, and I am happy with his service.

The only area of improvement is that since I had to coordinate with the Village, B&A could have been more detailed in their explanations on what was expected. Also, while giving out an estimate, give a final number so the customer can get a sense of the what it entails. Just quoting hourly rate isn't enough. I almost went with another company but decided to persist and get a total estimate. The final cost was lesser than the estimate which was a nice surprise.

Overall, 5 stars and I will call them in the future in case I need service. Price was reasonable, I paid by check to avoid a 3.5% fee. It's great to support a local Schaumburg business!

reviews.author: Laurie Jezuit
reviews.text: These guys are SO GREAT. My garbage disposal FELL DOWN (yikes!) and they were able to come at exactly the time I needed. Bobby and Ilga helped me over the phone, and Dean knew exactly what to do - he installed a new one and made sure everything was working. I feel so much better now!

reviews.author: Laura Davey
reviews.text: So happy with my experience working with B & A plumbing!  From the start Ilga was so helpful and kind and then when Dean and Jesus came out they were wonderful!  Dean is so calming and knowledgeable and knew exactly what to do!  In addition, he very patiently answered so many of my questions and addressed my concerns with empathy and expertise.  He is a great asset to your business and customers.  Thank you all for being great to work with!  I will definitely recommend you to others!

reviews.author: Jim “Cyberhymie” Conrad
reviews.text: They apparently don't warrant some of their work. When we had the same problem happen anew less than a week after they completed the work we hired them to do, they charged us more money and said the prior work wasn't covered by any warranty!

reviews.author: Marie P.
reviews.text:
Not happy with the quality of the repair I received in 2021. I called b and a to replace a 42 year old simple backyard spigot, it was leaking. 
Two young men came replaced spigot and the interior copper pipe. The repair had a one year warranty. 
One and  a half years later the spigot was pouring out water from the exterior vacuum seal. B and A would not come out and look at it unless I paid $182.00. They told me I must have left the hose on during the winter. No I did not. The last water source and copper pipe lasted 42 years! The old one should have caused serious problems long ago. I am a senior and really trusted that B and A would stand behind their work since they were a local company. I was so wrong. The end result was the interior pipe was split and I had water in my utility room. I regret changing the original spigot and regret trusting B and A .

reviews.author: Kathy G.
reviews.text: Let me start by stating that I typically never write reviews and my husband usually takes care of all repairs in the house. After discovering we had a hole in a pipe in our wall on a Sunday, my husband decided this is more that he really wanted to tackle. After clean up and a temporary fix to get us through to Monday, he made 4 calls to 4 companies based on reviews from the local FB site. One call back asked us to send pics and then he backed off, another said he could maybe stop by later in the day & to call when him back in the late afternoon (code for no thx), the third was in Elgin and was trying to see who'd be available to come to Schaumburg and then we got the call back from B&A.  They scheduled an appt to come out Tues morning.  They showed up on time as promised and got to work.  The initial problem was address and repaired quickly.  We then discovered the issue was bigger than we originally thought.  Corrosion in one pipe meant problems with the others.  Ultimately they had to schedule a second appt to break into the concrete to make the fix.  They came back as promised and fixed the issue. It was the best case scenario thankfully!  I was scared to look at the bill for the two visits but it was honestly a great surprise.  They were very reasonable and the total came in less then the deductible on our homeowners policy! A big thank you to Jim & Ryan for a job well done!  I highly recommend B&A!

reviews.author: Todd Jensen
reviews.text:
Updated review:
B & A Plumbing continues to provide great service!  Ian came to our house to address a rather tricky laundry tub drain issue and he was extremely friendly and professional.  Everything was explained so that we could understand the challenges involved to resolve the problem.  We have received consistent quality service from B & A for a number of years now and would highly recommend them for any and all plumbing needs.

Wow!  B & A Plumbing really came through for us today.  I am visiting my parents from out-of-town this week and we noticed that a downlight on the ground floor of the house was dripping water after running the upstairs shower.  We feared that the problem could be significant, however we decided to reach out to B & A on a Sunday and Bobby was able to come out shortly after we made the call.

Bobby was very courteous and quickly assessed the situation after cutting a small piece of drywall from the ceiling.  The leaking P-Trap (which was copper and over 50 years old) was removed and replaced with very little disruption to our day.

I can’t recommend B & A enough and we will always be grateful for Bobby coming to the rescue!

reviews.author: Corinne Z.
reviews.text: If I could give a half star I would.  I have used B&A before and while the plumbers themselves were very nice and professional the pricing seems to be way off.  They charged me $1700+ for a Reheem 40 gallon water heater (not high-effeciency).  Total bill was $2025. That night I checked Home Depot's website and could see that what I paid $1700+ for could have been purchased at HD for something in the $600-$700 range.  I understand a mark-up but $1,000+?!  When I called B&A the next day their answer was 'you should have/could have purchased the water heater from Home Depot'.   I spoke with a seasoned plumber who confirmed that I was overcharged.  I trusted them to give me good service (which they did) and expectd a competitive price (which they most certainly did not).  Never again.  I highly recommend you stay away from B&A Plumbing.

reviews.author: Stacy H
reviews.text:
Absolutely Outstanding Service!

B&A Plumbing was beyond amazing! From start to finish, their team was extremely courteous, professional, and understanding. We were so impressed by how quickly they were able to fit us in — they came out the very next day!

The plumber arrived right on time, diagnosed the issue quickly, and walked us through every step of the process with clear, easy-to-understand explanations. They resolved the problem efficiently and left us feeling completely confident and taken care of.

It’s rare these days to find such responsive and respectful service. We felt heard, helped, and totally supported throughout the entire experience.

Highly, highly, highly recommend B&A Plumbing! If you want honest, skilled professionals who go above and beyond — look no further! 🙌

reviews.author: Ike H.
reviews.text:
Toilet clogged and water started to overflow, wetting the entire floor and the basement ceiling underneath, and this all happened at 1:00am on Friday night.
The basement wetting was a concern, and didn't want to risk unclogging the toiled myself fearing there might be some unknown leaks in the pipes.

Saw that B&A was open 24hrs so I called, and the call center lady was very nice accommodating. I figured I'd ask for a call first thing in the morning, but Bobby called about 10min later. I explained the situation, asked him if he can come earl morning, and he did. He came on time, fixed the toilet, confirmed that there are other leaks, and charged me 2/3hrs even though there's usually an 1hr minimum.

Thank you Bobby
Thank you B&A Plumming 
Now I see why they have such a high review.

reviews.author: Manny Hernandez
reviews.text:
If you’re looking for plumbers in the Schaumburg area look no further. These guys have a very long history in Schaumburg (Family owned business) and are the most honest plumbers in the area. They won’t overcharge you or use any shady techniques (like most other places have from my experience), but most importantly- They get the job done. They are more than happy to work along with the Village of Schaumburg as well for Witness Rodding to make sure everything goes smoothly.

Not to mention, super great team! From setting up an appointment to getting my sewer lines rodded for roots, everyone from B&A was stellar and did a fantastic job. Shoutout to Dj and Derek for being such great guys and helping me with my sewage backup problem. Thank you again!

reviews.author: Nancy Hughes
reviews.text: My Brother-in-Law used B & A Plumbing and told me what a superior job this company provided, along with the price.  I knew they were from Schaumburg, I called to see if they'd service the Wheaton area and they do.  My shower did not have hot water and I needed someone.  I called and they were able to send someone the next day.  Bobby was professional, respectful, answered all my questions and took the necessary time that was needed to complete the project (no rushing). For what I needed, and the price they charged was very reasonable.   I would definitely recommend B & A Plumbing without any hesitation. And definitely request Bobby for my projects.  It was a pleasure to work with this Company!

reviews.author: Kelly L.
reviews.text: I realized on a Sunday night that my water heater was leaking, so I called Monday morning at 8:05 and B&A Plumbing was at my house at 8:30am with a new water heater.  It took about 3 hours to install because my piping was not to code, so they took care of everything!!  The price was moderate, but I have learned from past mistakes that the cheapest is not always the best!  The team was respectful, did a great job, and kept the area clean.  I was referred by a friend who used this company, and I would definitely refer this company out to everyone I know.  Thank you B&A Plumbing for preventing a future disaster!!

reviews.author: Andrew B.
reviews.text: My gas water heater pilot light wouldn't stay on. I called and they came by within a couple of hours of my call and were able to get it re-lit. They showed me what they did, explained the problem and what a replacement unit would cost. The plumber said that I would likely need to get it replaced due to the age and configuration if it went out again. Well, within a couple of hours the heater went off again and I could not get it to restart with their instructions, so I called back and was able to get them out same day to replace the heater. The work was done quickly and professionally, and at the quoted price.

reviews.author: David B.
reviews.text:
I had an issue with a toilet and and adjacent sink. I was afraid that there was a break in the common drain pipe after having had a similar problem a dozen years ago.

The plumber B&A dispatched was Mike Freier. He was very friendly, professional and competent. He worked quick and clean! The problem turned out to be a minor one, thankfully. He was done and out in an hour. And he gave advice on how to prevent the sink issue from recurring. He provided, by far, the best plumbing experience I have ever had.

If all the B&A plumbers are as good as Mike you would be silly to call anyone else.

synthesis.summary: B&A consistently undercuts competitors on price — multiple reviewers report quotes double what B&A charged — while showing up same-day or within hours even on weekends and holidays.
strengths: Pricing undercuts competitors significantly: at least 3 reviewers independently report other companies quoted double B&A's price for the same job
Fast dispatch even outside business hours: New Year's Day emergency, Friday afternoon broken valve fixed within 30 minutes, weekend shower backup resolved within 2 hours
Long-term customer loyalty is unusually strong — one household has used them since 1983, another 25 years, and an aging-home customer calls them repeatedly with full confidence in their integrity
weaknesses: Estimating process lacks transparency: one reviewer noted that quoting only an hourly rate without a total estimate made it hard to compare bids, and the process for coordinating with third parties (e.g., village water shutoff) wasn't explained upfront
synthesis.emergencyNotes: Strong emergency signals: documented New Year's Day burst pipe response, Friday 3pm broken valve fixed within 30 minutes, weekend sewer backup resolved within 2 hours, and an evening overtime call handled same night — this is a crew that actually picks up and dispatches.
synthesis.platformDiscrepancy: Google sits at 4.9 while Yelp is a meaningful 0.3 lower at 4.6, and the BBB shows a B- rating without accreditation — neither is alarming on its own, but the pattern suggests a small subset of customers had experiences that didn't match the majority.

reviews.text: Professional, friendly, and efficient! The plumbers from Five Guys Plumbing Schaumburg were very knowledgeable and made sure everything was working perfectly before leaving. I will definitely call them again for any future plumbing needs.

reviews.author: Lindsey Ward
reviews.text: I can’t recommend Five Guys Plumbing enough! From the first call to the job completion, everything was seamless. They were punctual, honest, and very skilled. My plumbing issue was resolved perfectly, and I’m very impressed by their service.

reviews.author: Michael Vargas
reviews.text: Horrible customer service.  I had a plumbing emergency and was told by "Lucas" that a plumber would be out early the following morning during an agreed upon time.  The next day I called to confirm and was told by Lucas that a plumber wouldn't be arriving until hours later despite what he told me the day before.  I expressed my displeasure explaining how the water damage was making drywall fall off in chunks.  Lucas told me that's "not an emergency" and "it's no problem".  He had no answer for why he promised one thing but couldn't deliver on it.  Then instead of trying to turn this into a customer service success story he rudely hung up on me.  You're a real hero, Lucas.  Zero stars.

reviews.author: ปริยวิศว์ สุขธยารักษ์
reviews.text: I had a great experience with Five Guys Plumbing Schaumburg and highly recommend their services. Their team was professional, friendly, and quick to respond. Scheduling an appointment was easy, and they arrived on time, fully prepared for the job. The plumber was knowledgeable and took the time to assess my issue before explaining the best solution. Their pricing was fair and transparent, with no hidden fees. They quickly repaired my leaking pipe and also fixed a clogged drain in my bathroom. The quality of their work was excellent, and they ensured everything was working perfectly before leaving. I was impressed by their attention to detail and how clean they left my space. Finding a reliable plumber can be difficult, but Five Guys Plumbing Schaumburg exceeded my expectations. If you need plumbing repairs, installations, or maintenance, this is the company to call. Their dedication to quality and customer satisfaction is outstanding. I will definitely be using their services again in the future.

reviews.author: Jaelynn Macie
reviews.text: Five Guys Plumbing Schaumburg provided excellent and reliable service. The plumber arrived right on time, quickly identified the problem, and fixed it efficiently with great attention to detail. They were professional, courteous, and upfront about pricing, which I really appreciated. The work area was left clean, and everything is running perfectly now. I would definitely recommend Five Guys Plumbing Schaumburg to anyone needing trustworthy plumbing services.

Spoke with Lucas needing service - asked me for contact info which I provided - said he would stop by - didn’t - text for follow up - never heard back. Must not need the business 😑

Customers appreciate their punctuality, attention to detail, and thorough workmanship. Highly recommended for anyone in need of dependable plumbing solutions.

reviews.author: SHIRLEY NICOL LEON VASQUEZ
reviews.text: I’m very happy with the work done by Five Guys Plumbing Schaumburg. From scheduling the appointment to finishing the repair, everything was easy and stress-free. The plumber was professional, courteous, and very skilled at his job. They made sure everything was working perfectly before leaving. Truly reliable and trustworthy service!

reviews.author: 501-เนตรนภา-03
reviews.text: A leaking pipe in the kitchen caused water damage under the sink. The service included locating the leak, replacing the damaged pipe, and testing the system for proper water flow. All work was completed efficiently, leaving the plumbing fully functional and preventing any further water issues.

reviews.author: Hector Gaddy
reviews.text: This plumber was fantastic. They were at the top of their game and their prices were quite fair. I had to summon them a few times, but each time they came right away and handled the situation for me. These guys were great and we will be using them again. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Roberto Logan
reviews.text: Outstanding service! The plumber arrived on time, located the issue right away, and fixed it much faster than I expected. Very professional, clean work, and fair pricing. It’s refreshing to deal with someone who knows what they’re doing and treats customers with respect.

reviews.author: Fitzgerald Levi
reviews.text: A truly dependable and trustworthy company. Their work ethic and professionalism are remarkable. It’s refreshing to see a team so dedicated to providing great results. I’ll definitely continue doing business with them and won’t hesitate to recommend them to others.

reviews.text: He discovered a leak in the bathroom's drainpipe, and the cost to replace them was not excessive. They performed a fantastic job replacing the pipes when they returned. charged us a fair fee and made sure that our pipes were flawless when they departed.

reviews.text: He detected a leak in the drainpipe to the bathroom and the cost for replacing them was not bad at all. When they came back to replace the pipes they did a great job. Made sure our pipes were perfect before they left, and charged a great price.

synthesis.summary: Consistently fast, clean work with transparent pricing — but one documented emergency dispatch failure where a dispatcher promised a morning arrival, then moved the window hours later and hung up on a customer with active water damage.
strengths: Speed on-site: at least 5 reviewers specifically call out faster-than-expected arrival or same-day response, including a burst pipe and a sink overflow handled within hours
Transparent, fair pricing: 4+ reviewers independently mention upfront or honest pricing without being prompted, including on a water heater leak and pipe replacement
Thorough job completion: multiple reviewers note plumbers tested everything and cleaned up before leaving, not just fixing and walking out
weaknesses: Emergency dispatch communication broke down in at least one documented case — a customer was given a confirmed morning window, then told hours later it had shifted, with no explanation and the call ending in a hang-up
redFlags: The 1-star review describes a dispatcher named 'Lucas' who promised an arrival time, changed it without notice during an active water damage emergency, dismissed the urgency by saying 'it's not an emergency,' and hung up — this is a direct contradiction of the responsiveness pattern seen elsewhere and suggests inconsistent dispatch quality
synthesis.emergencyNotes: Multiple reviews confirm rapid response to true emergencies including a burst basement pipe and a sink overflow, with one reviewer saying they 'came right out' and resolved the issue before significant damage — but the one negative review is specifically an emergency dispatch failure, so after-hours reliability cannot be fully guaranteed.

reviews.author: Ieasha Mccullough
reviews.text: So grateful for Mike! He did an excellent job explaining what the possible reasons for my sink backup could be and an even greater job providing me with reasonable and affordable solutions. Extremely satisfied with the service provided. Got my water flowing and sink draining in no time! Huge thank you to MIke!

reviews.author: immari hysaw
reviews.text: Mike at Roto-Rooter did a fantastic job! Took time to explain the process, periodically informed me of his progress, resolved the issue and cleaned up after himself. Got here quickly and completed the job quickly as well. Highly Recommend!

reviews.author: Jeff Therkelsen
reviews.text: Mike, my technician, was awesome. He was extremely courteous and kept me informed throughout the repair. Mine was a very difficult main drain to open. He put every effort into clearing it. He just wouldn’t give up. I’m sure many other companies would have thrown in the towel and recommended that I call an excavator. Not Mike; he kept at it until he was able to clear it out. There is one set fee and he gave me that upfront. And then he proceeded to spend four hours working on it. This is the second time that I’ve needed their service and was more than satisfied with their. On a scale of one to five they are a ten!

reviews.author: Michael Touhy
reviews.text:
We had sewage coming up from our basement laundry drain and called Roto Rooter to help us. They did anything but. Eddie arrived on site and called in his supervisor, Max Corner. Max said that he was unable to open up the main basement clean out so they had to run equipment from the main floor bathroom. This added 8-10’ to how far they attempted to rod which apparently weakened their equipment enough that they were not able to properly determine where the actual damage was. Max drew up a proposal and told me once I signed they would be able to get a crew out the next day to begin work. I signed the contract trying to get my home back in order and Max then called to tell me they actually wouldn’t be able to start the next day because he had already left and did not map out the yard (never received an explanation as to why this was not done when he was on site). He returned the next day and due to the cold weather he could not get his equipment or spray paint to work leading him to pace my yard yelling curse words for 20+ minutes getting to the point where a neighbor had to call and ask if everything was ok at the house. Max then came back in to do the same inside because he was not able to get the toilet back on (photo attached). He left it like this and said it was fine because it wasn’t actively leaking.
The next day a crew was supposed to arrive by 10am and they showed up around 2pm. They dug a hole and cracked my line and despite this area not being the issue, put in a clean out and left. Public Works actually told them that that do not appear to be the issue spot and they told him that that was the spot they were contracted to dig. They sent in a jetter who said that the issue was actually 8-10’ farther down the line and max would have to come back. The jetter also would not hook up his equipment to the main line because it was only accessible under my porch and he would not go under there. So he cut a hole in my basement window screen and hooked up to a near 100 year old laundry tub which is now leaking.
Max came back and confirmed that the issue was actually 10’ farther down the line and immediately quoted me an additional $7000 even though I was already out $8500 FOR WORK THAT DID NOT HAVE TO BE DONE!
I told him that I was not going to use them and called a local plumber who said that the job was actually $3500.
I’m getting in touch with an attorney as I now have more damage than when I called in Roto Rooter and they did unnecessary work for which they overcharged.

reviews.author: Sue F.
reviews.text:
We had these guys out for an estimate on replacing our sewer line and fixing our ejector pump. They gave us an estimate of 10,000 to replace the ejector pump, citing it was a commercial grade pump and they would have to dig a new pit in order to replace it. 

After getting estimate from 3 other companies, each of them told me the same.  The ejector pump did not need to be replaced.  Ejector pumps very rarely need to be replaced.   It was an electrical problem and I should contact an electrician to get it repaired.  

They can another totally way high estimate to replace the sewer line (about triple other companies estimate).  

They charged for the estimate too. 

They get the rating for being unethical and charging exorbitant amounts of money for their service

reviews.author: Patrick K.
reviews.text:
It all started when my bathtub started filling up with gross water.  My wife and I wanted to go with Roto-Rooter because they seemed to be a reputable business and have been around a long time.  Their response to our problem was very quick.  We called them in the morning and they had someone the next day.  

The first tech they sent worked his butt off.  He was out rodding my front yard for several hours.  After a while he told us the line was not only clogged, but it appears to be broken in at least 1 spot.  He said he cleared the line good enough to use it for things like flushing toilets and taking showers. However, this was an issue that need more attention.  He said he would call his supervisor and that the supervisor would be out tomorrow.

The next day the supervisor arrived an hour after our scheduled time.  He seemed very knowledgeable about the issue and said he had been doing this 10 years.

He ran a camera down and showed us all the issues.  He gave us a quote of 10k+.  This was an unexpected expense but it was a major issue and since Roto-Rooter had a good name, my wife and decided to go with them.

The supervisor showed up on a Monday to have me sign off on the paperwork and said the job would start the next day between 8-10.  This was a 1 day job possibly 2 if there is an issue.

DAY 1The crew showed up roughly around 11 am.  The workers set things up duh holes for the pipe and then left....For approx 2 hours.  When the workers returned they worked for another hour or so

The crew came back around 3 and worked for another hour or so.  Towards the end of the day around 4, one of the workers knocked on my door to tell me they were done for the day.  I looked to the street and noticed water was running from my house down the curb all the way down the street.  The worker stated he hit my outgoing sewer line but it was ok, I still had running water.  He said water would stop running out once the pipe emptied.

After the workers left I evaluated the job site to find the holes they had dug left uncovered and caution tape hanging on by a thread.

DAY 2 The next morning, one of the holes filled up with water.  The hole was approximately 4' deep and nothing safely covering them.  I called the supervisor and told him that the crew needs to come here immediatelty fix up, I live around alot of families with children who could get hurt.  In the meantime, the city came to my door saying that the  water that was still running was actually the water hookup for the city.  The city shut my water off around 12.

The workers showed up around 10:30 covered the holes and left around 1 after the water had been shut off.  The workers would return around 3.  At approx 4:30 they knocked on my door to let me know they had found the issue but unfortunately the water would have to stay off for the remainder of the night.  They did offer my a hotel room which at that point was not what I wanted to hear.

I voiced my concerns to the supervisor that sold me the job and he said he understood my concern but couldnt do anything that day.  I requested a new set of workers because I was worried this expensive job was not being handled properly.  The supevisor said he would look into it.

DAY 3 The same workers showed up.  I called the supervisor and he said he didn't want to rock the boat with the workers or they may walk off the job and I wouldnt be able to get things fixed.  The water was turned on that day.  However the job was not completed.

DAY 4 The workers showed up at their normal time and said the job would most likely get done today.  However, by this point, the city was on to the job at my house and they were making regular visits to make sure the job was being done correctly.  The job was not completed

DAY 5 This was actually a Monday so I had these large exposed holes all weekend.  However, they were covered properly.  The job was finished and approved by the city that day.

CONCLUSION My wife and I are heartbroken and extremely upset by the lack of consideration for my community and the people living in it as well as the response by Roto Rooter themselves when called out.  During my frustration, I contacted the BBB and reported Roto Rooter as at this point, the supervisor I had been speaking with seemed to keep getting me the run around.  Roto-Rooter's response was pretty much "We did our job correctly, JULIE marked the lines wrong, so blame them"  They never addressed and of my other concerns.  

At no time was the supervisor that had sold me the job or any other representative from Roto-Rooter called me or showed up to the job site to address my concerns.  On top of that, when I spoke to the supervisor I had been working with, he really made it sound like all the work that had been done was a band-aid solution and realistically, we may have to dig up the line completely if it happens again.  A 10k+ band-aid.  Thats the work I paid for and the terrible service I received.

reviews.author: Eric S.
reviews.text:
We've used Roto-Rooter to clean out our sewer line as it periodically gets jammed up with root growth every few years.  In 2011 the tech was great, did good work and I was happy with the job.  So happy that I didn't think twice about who to call when we started getting some backup and it was time to get the line cleaned out again.

Quite a different experience this time.  I made an appointment online and selected the 10a-12p window.  Around 11:30 the dispatcher called to let me know the crews were working in the area but running behind.  ETA probably another hour.  Another hour or so passed and another call from dispatch with the same story and this time no ETA to give.  Finally at 2:30 dispatch called to say the tech was en route.

Another hour passes, and around 3:30 I called the dispatcher to ask where the tech was at.  Was told he was real close and he finally arrived shortly afterwards.

First thing I'm asked is if I have a clean-out he can tap into outside of the house.  I told him no it's in the utility room, I've got it open and the area clear and you are all set.  He asks me how long I've lived in my house and, after I tell him, lectures me that "You've lived here 12 years you should have had a cleanout installed outside the house".  For fun apparently.  Or maybe to make the Roto-Rooter guy's life easier.  I explained to him that every other Roto-Rooter guy has been able to do the job without issue from the same cleanout he'd be using.

Next complaint was that he would have to bring his 'big heavy machine' down a short flight of six stairs into my finished basement (again, same as every other roto-rooter guy ever has) because - you guessed it - I never had an exterior clean-out installed.

Finally getting around to looking at the cleanout in the utility room, I'm advised that it's only a 3 inch pipe and that the line by the street is 6 inches.  If I had a (you knew this was coming) 6 inch clean-out installed in any of the last 12 years like I should have, this wouldn't be a problem but as it stands he will only be able to cut a 3 inch hole through the clog.  Also the rusty pipe cap was in dismal shape (it is) and he might not be able to get it back on in which case the pipe would leak inside the wall.  His predecessor has simply smashed plumber's putty around the cap which served its purpose for over two years, which I pointed out.  He wasn't sure he had any plumber's putty.  The guy who works with plumbing for a living...

At this point I lost my patience.  I told him that if he didn't feel he could do the job or planned on leaving me with a mess to deal with afterwards, he could leave and I'd work with another company.  He stopped lecturing, gave me a release form to sign "so I am not responsible for any problems after the job", and went out to drag in his rodding machine.

I called Roto-Rooter management to ask what sort of person they'd sent over.  Got a nice explanation about why the rusty cap on my pipe was no good and how they see this all the time and how having a cleanout installed outside would be a good idea and basically a lot of talk that boiled down to a politer version of the attitude I was already getting from the tech.  Apology for the tech's attitude?  No.  Apology for blowing an appointment window by 3.5 hours?  No.

So the guy did the job and my clog was removed.  He tried to sell me a $20 replacement cap for the pipe, but the ones he had wouldn't fit.  So in the end, he had to use plumber's putty to seal it back on just like the other roto-rooter guys.
Turns out he had had some sitting in his truck the entire time.  Of course it had also frozen solid and couldn't be used.  So - I had to give him a container of mine.

The coup de grace was having to help him carry his big, heavy machine out of the basement.

After he left I spent another half hour cleaning dirt (yeah right) stains off the utility room tile and the basement carpet.  I also have a large, frozen puddle of 'dirt' on my driveway that leaked out of the rodding machine.

This is probably the worst experience I have ever had with a services company.  I used to work construction with my dad as a kid, so I'm aware of and sympathetic to a lot of the nightmare situations these guys have to deal with in people's houses I and tend to cut them a lot of slack.  Even showing up hours late - god knows what he got caught up in that he couldn't walk away from all morning.  No problem.  

But in the end, when I spend my entire day cooped up waiting for someone to show up and charge me $350 for 45 minutes of work - I don't need any attitude whatsoever and I expect them to be able to do the job correctly, with their own tools and without causing me any sort of headaches along the way.

reviews.author: Eric F.
reviews.text:
First time single family home owner here.  I have no idea what I'm doing yet.  Had an unexpected water back up and called one of the only places who answered at 6:30 pm on Thursday night.  That's why they get the 1 star.  They came out promptly.  They didn't call to confirm but they showed up so that was cool.  

First guy was nice.  He sort of explained things.  He kind of laughed as he had me sign the document saying it was 435 to rod from a clean out outside in front to the main line.  The internet says this is a ridiculous price but I had 435 dollars and I had an issue so I signed the form.  He worked for several hours until his machine failed.  He indicated he knew he had issues but had hoped the machine would make it through to the weekend.  I thought this was pretty unprofessional.  He also cut the cable and left a 30 foot metal cable covered in sewage in my front yard.  I guess I get to figure out what to do with that now.  So I now had to take the following day off work to meet with guy number two.  

Guy number two came out and he was also courteous.  He worked for a while and warned me (early on which was obviously a sales tactic) that he felt I may have a collapsed pipe somewhere in the main line.  I immediately hit google for additional info and to prepare myself for whatever bs was about to come next.  They sent a third guy with a camera out.  He showed me the tree roots on the camera and talked about how bad they were and gave me two options.  (Third guy commented on how they would get the metal crap cable out of my yard but they haven't done that yet and its now Tuesday.)    

One, have some guy with a high pressure machine that shoots water through the system that eliminates issues the first tools they had couldn't get.  Camera guy/supervisor expressed this as the only next logical option which would indicate whether or not I needed to go to option 2 I will get to in a minute.  This water pressure guy charges 550 an hour but Roto Rooter will have him cap the cost at 800 just for me.  Read that saturated with sarcasm.  Look up what that service costs elsewhere.  This was complete garbage and literally this company is now just taking advantage of me.  They called the guy and advised him to come over under this assumed close situation.  I am a saleseperson but I don't know anything about plumbing.  I was starting to panic as 435 became 1235 and was potentially about to become:

Option two: 

Lets rip your yard and driveway up and replace the entire line with this way stronger material for an insane number of dollars.            

Between the time the second guy left and the water pressure guy was about to head over... I had a plumber I know and trust become available.  He advised me to call off water pressure guy and said he would head over.  He came over with a heavier duty version of the tool the first two dudes used.  He cleared the obstruction in 35 minutes and wrapped up and my problem was resolved.  He charged me 200 dollars.

At the end of the day, I wish I had the foresight to emergency call the guy I knew instead of calling Roto Rooter during a panic mode.  They would have easily spent 5 times what I should have spent and wasted a ton of my time.  It's unfortunate that companies with names you recognize survive by capitalizing on inexperienced homeowners and a person's trust.  They don't deserve your trust.  They spent 435 of my dollars and 6 hours of my time and didn't actually fix anything and, in fact left a metal cable, covered in feces and grease in my front yard.

Edit: 

Within moments of me posting this review, a representative responded on here.  I emailed them and they called me.  They offered solutions that made me feel a lot more comfortable about potentially using them in the future.  

Situations can go sideways in any business.  The company itself is apparently very attentive to their clients needs and personal and financial situations.  I can certainly appreciate them for making the difficult call reaching out and I applaud them for taking the steps necessary to avoid others from having similar negative experiences.

reviews.author: JoVie W.
reviews.text:
I am writing this review because I want to warn people about Roto Rooter.  I called Roto Rooter because I was experiencing water overflowing from my toilet during heavy rainfalls.  Roto Rooter was late for the first appointment, however, I must say that they did call and were pretty good about keeping me in the loop in regards to when a plumber would be available.  The plumber did arrive, about an hour late. He informed me that I needed a camera inspection and that he was not prepared to do that.  He also said that he was only an emergency plumber and only prepared to rod out the sewer line.  He made an appointment for the next day for a camera inspection.

Next day...The plumber did arrive on time.  The plumber came equipped with an inspection camera and was ready to rod the sewer line.  It was determined that I had roots in my sewer line and that rodding was necessary.  The plumber preceeded to rod out the sewer line.  About 5 mins into rodding he told me that he thought my sewer line was busted and that I may have a broken pipe (1 strike).  I started to freak out and asked for verification.  He told me he would verify after rodding was complete.  He continued to rod the sewer line but kept insisting that the roots were too thick and that he "hoped" he could get through them.  I watched him rod out my sewer.  He was able to get through with the 2 inch attachment but was not able to advance much with the 4 inch.  He said the roots were too aggressive (this process took about 20 mins, including set up). 

He performed a camera inspection after he decided that rodding was not going to work.  The camera inspection did not identify any broken pipes but I could see the roots.  The roots were located on the city property but he told me that I had to have a clean out valve installed on my property to fix the issue.  A $500 job just turned into a $4500 job for a city issue (strike 2).  I asked him why he could not install a clean out valve on the city's side because that is where the issue was.  I wanted to know why he thought it necessary to tear my lawn apart.  He then told me that if I wanted to get the city involved it would cost me an additional $650 to enter the Private Drains Program (which is free by the way if you look it up on the city's website).  He also informed me that it would take the city about 3 to 4 weeks to respond and that he didn't think I had that amount of time.  He also told me that he didn't think that I should use my water (strike 3)! 

At this point, I felt like the plumber was just trying to rip me off and told him thank you for your services and paid him $400 bucks for a camera inspection (he told me he didn't charge me for rodding ....yeah okay!!). I called the city and they said a permit would be $250 and that an inspector would come out the within a week.  The licensed plumber who came 2 days later was able to unclog the sewer line, without any issues, within one hour.  He also used rodding to clear out the sewer line!  I did NOT NEED A CLEAN OUT VALVE WHICH WOULD HAVE COST ME $4500!!! All the original plumber needed to do was try a little hard to get his equipment through.  It's not as if he didn't have time on his hands to do it.  He sat at my house for an additional 2 hours waiting for the finance guy (so that I could finance the $4500) and listening to him reassure me that a clean out valve was necessary.

Beware of being ripped off my Roto Rooter!

reviews.author: Eve H.
reviews.text:
I am writing this  review at the request of Roto Rooter. At the end of the repair the repair man handed me of a flyer that said, "write a review get a refund." But I don't think he counted on the fact that I was unhappy with Roto Rooter they caused a leak in my pipe. 
I called Roto Rooter to get my pipes rodded out after my handyman said that he was unable to fix the slow drain. Before my handyman left he showed me where the pipe needed to be rotted out. He  told me they should not use the drain in the sink because there were too many bends in
 The pipes and they would break the them causing a leak. When the repair man from Roto Rooter  arrived I showed him where he should get into the pipe in the basement. The repair man said oh no I'm going to do it from the kitchen sink, I said , but there are so many bends in the pipe, aren't you afraid of causing a leak? He stated that he knew what he was doing. Before the repair man began he gave me a paper to sign I thought it was just to okay the amount I was going to be charged and giving them permission to rod out the drain. What it was he later told was a disclaimer stating they were not responsible for causing any leaks in the pipes. The workman asked me to watch the pipes in the basement and tell him when he reached a bend in the so he wouldn't create a leak. When he started threading the rodder through the pipe it immediately started to shake and make a loud noise. I told him to stop,  he said he barely had the rodder in the pipe and continued to try to fish the rodder through the pipe. When he finished he told me I had a leak in the pipe in the wall near the sink. This seemed very strange to me since I never had a leak there before Roto Rooter was in my house. The repairman tried to fix the leak with some kind of wax. I called Roto Rooter and reported the leak caused by the Roto Rooter repairman. The lady said they would send someone else out to repair the leak and replace the pipe. I asked if there was a charge and she said no. When the new repairman arrived he informed me I signed a disclaimer and wanted $750.00 to replace the pipe. I said they should repair it for free, the repairman told me he spoke to the first repairman who said I had signed the disclaimer, but he neglected to tell him it had been given to me surreptitiously. I did not have this man replace the pipe, I had someone else fix it  for $350.
I do not recommend Roto Rooter at all but,I had to give them one star since that Is the lowest Yelp will allow me to give.

reviews.author: Eric L.
reviews.text:
I had a problem on Sunday 9/7/14 with a sink drain that was clogged.  I called Roto Rooter and made an appointment for Monday.  The plumber came out and looked at it and told me the drain needed to be rodded to clear the blockage.  I have never had this done, so I had no idea what it was going to cost.  The guy showed me a book and told me it would be $469.  Not knowing what this service cost, I agreed to let him do the work.  Ironically, later that day I received a Valpak in the mail with a coupon for a local plumber that offered power rodding for $50 with no trip charge.  Obviously I got screwed.  The plumber was there for one hour, so $469 for an hour of work seems outrageous.  I will never use Roto Rooter again, and I will make sure everyone I know is told about this experience.  This is totally unacceptable, clearly they are taking advantage of an uneducated homeowner.  I could have even handled three times what the other plumber charges, but almost 10 times the charge is just plain screwing people.  Here is the funny thing, I just looked up the cost of the power rodding equipment on Global Industries website, an almost identical piece of equipment costs $563 brand new.  So what exactly does Roto Rooter do, use it a couple of times and throw it away?  That is the only explanation for this kind of charge.

Follow up:
I called a couple of local plumbers and the average price to Rod a drain was $115 for a kitchen sink.  Therefore I called Roto Rooter to complain.  I was told the price is set by the national home office and there is no negotiation in the price.  They also told me that I was charged $59 for a gallon of enzyme to help keep the drain clean.  I did get this bottle of stuff, but was never told I would be charged for it.  I told them I did not want it, so they said they would schedule a time to come pick it up and give me a credit.  The manager ended the call by saying, "I hope this makes you happy."  Seriously?  I got charged 4 times as much as the average price, plus was charged for a product I never requested, and you think I'm going to be happy?  Do not use Roto Rooter, they will scam you.  Call a local plumber who is fair and honest.

reviews.author: Jaime R.
reviews.text:
The first contact was via email and online.  It was positive.
They advertise free estimates.  When the plumber arrived, the free estimate was over $400 to rod the sewer line or over $300 to use the camera and video the line. I guess they should advertise that the free estimate is to tell you how much it will cost to tell you what needs to be done.  Creative way to mislead the customers.

Once the video was completed, I was told that I had 2 problems and it would cost almost $9,000 to fix it.  The problems were a leaky sewer line connection and a sewer line collapsing.  Basically they need to dig two areas, one about 4 feet and another about 6 feet and replace a couple of pipes, T connector and clean out.  I estimate this should take no more than 12 hours.  So, 12 hours at $750 per hour, not bad.  I want to be a plumber now. By the way, all other plumbers confirmed that it should not take more than 12 hours of work.  When I told the plumber that the cost was too high, he told me that there might be a way to repair the line without digging by patching the pipe.  He told me and wrote on the estimate that he had to talk to his supervisor, Kris, to confirm and he would call me the next day to confirm.  He never called me back, so they lost the business.

Next chapter - I called four other plumbers.  All of them suggested another way to correct the leaky line by replacing the pipe at another area to make sure the problem was fixed right. The final cost was way under half of what Roto-Rooter quoted.

I  do not recommend this company.

12-2-14 Review update.

I was contacted by the customer service team and they sent my comments to Lynnette who called me and we had a productive discussion about the service call. She refunded the full amount of the service call and assured me that Roto-Rooter appreciates my business and wants to keep me as a customer.  I was satisfied by the way she handled it.  I will try them again in the future.  Thanks for listening and for taking care of your customers. I appreciate it.

reviews.author: Lily T.
reviews.text:
I would rate my experience ZERO stars!!! We hired them to do some water mitigation in our basement. First thing the project manager wanted to see was our home owners insurance. Ooh your house has a great policy. Hmm why would he say that?? Red flag #1. We file a claim with our insurance. He tells us that he will send his best team. Next day 2 guys show up and ask what can be thrown out. Me: umm I want to save as much as we can as these are important to my family. Oh ok,
Note: we had original artwork stored in a storage room. We also had 10 folding tables that could have been used. Instead the two guys placed 14 pieces of original art on the wet floor of the basement along with the 14 easels and numerous boxes of personal items that originally were not on the floor but ended up on the floor. Removed
Baseboard/trim and flooring. Sprayed cleaner on the floor. Put a bunch of air movers on the floor, installed a separate circuit for movers. Then they didn't plug them into the separate circuit and blew out AC circuit. Couple of days later we had a major storm in our neighborhood. No power for over 25 hrs.  6 inches of water in the basement and personal items on the floor and original art damaged!Called pm who said we don't work with people who have no power call us back when you do. Umm you are billing yourself as water mitigation but you definitely are NOT. Hired another more reputable company who came
and cleaned up the mess that was made by your team. Insurance paid out a significant porting of your invoice. Why would we pay the remaining balance when you destroyed personal property during your time in our house? If anyone is looking at water cleanup or mitigation this is one company to stay far far away from! More crazy details too much to post and I'm too angry to write about but heed my words stay away from this company!

reviews.author: Jonathan O.
reviews.text:
I don't often write reviews, but in this instance I feel I may be able to help someone in the future.
We had a root problem causing sewage backup in our basement.  We were having other work done at our house through a trusted contractor, so we asked for his help.
He and his crew tried to get the roots out but were unsuccessful with the device they rented from Home Depot.  
The contractor then called Roto Rooter to come out and take a video of what was in the pipe and try to resolve the issue.  

One good thing about the experience is that Roto Rooter was out at our house right away with our contractor. (My wife and I were at work).  After taking a video and looking at the footage, Roto Rooter tried to clear the roots for about 30 minutes to no avail.  This charge was $550.

Then, according to our contractor, the two gentlemen were very bold saying that this should be taken care of immediately and that they will be back this afternoon to rip up the driveway and clear out the roots.  The price quoted for this was $8,000. Luckily our contractor didn't agree and sent them off and called us immediately and advised us to get another opinion.  
After 3 attempts to have the video footage emailed to us, we received it and reviewed it with a couple local plumbers who were not pleased that Roto Rooter wanted to rip up our driveway.
We hired one of them and they cleared the roots within 15-20 minutes with a 3" blade, then went back through with a 4" blade.  They had the issue resolved within less than an hour and guaranteed their work for a year and advised us to have it cleared at least every other year to prevent this from happening again.  

Long story short, get a second opinion.  It could very well save you thousands of dollars.

reviews.author: Jeff T.
reviews.text:
Back in September my toilets weren't flushing fully and there was a sewer type smell in the kitchen.  The Roto-Rooter technician spent all day rooting the lines.  After a full day, and $400.00 later, he told me he did the best he could but it's still not working and I should call his manager.  He was kind enough to leave a Roto-Rooter pen behind but he left it in the back of my toilet!!!!  No kidding, I found it when I lifted the lid off the back.  James came to my home with a camera.  He recommended a pipe patch at the shift and installation of a clean out access between the city and driveway even though I had one in the back yard.

$7,000.00 later and the same problem.  They refunded the initial $400.00 charge for rooting but I was still out $6,600.00.  James had a few different guys come to re root but still no luck.  After several frustrating days James came back with more cameras and a plumber.  They eventually cleared the lines but I wonder if the clean out was necessary as I already had one in the back yard.  The smell remained.

This time they said my problem was broken cast iron under a toilet even though the camera couldn't show it.  No problem, they were willing to rip my floor apart, replace the cast iron, install PVC replacement for the tub and clean the area for a measly $7,500.00.

This time I sought a second opinion.  Guess what?  NO CRACK IN THE CAST IRON!  The problem was a cracked pipe in my kitchen sink.  This legitimate plumber replaced it for $1,800.00  I later found someone to sanitize the area for $1,500.00.

Lesson learned, go with local family owned companies!!!!

synthesis.summary: They'll show up fast — sometimes within an hour — but multiple reviewers report supervisors pushing $5,000–$15,000 in unnecessary repairs that second-opinion plumbers either solved for a fraction of the cost or said weren't needed at all.
strengths: Fast response documented across multiple reviews, including one reviewer noting a tech arrived within an hour of calling
Several individual technicians (Mike, Luis, Manny) praised by name for persistence, cleanup, and clear communication on straightforward jobs
At least one reviewer confirms upfront flat-fee pricing was honored even after a 4-hour job on a difficult drain
weaknesses: Pricing runs significantly above market: reviewers report $365 for 12 minutes of work, $550–$600 for simple drain clogs that competitors charge $150–$325 for, and $8,300–$8,500 for pipe repairs later replicated by local plumbers for $1,800–$3,500

Work quality inconsistent and job-dependent: multiple reviews describe techs leaving damage, failing to complete the job, or making problems worse — including a tech leaving a toilet unbolted, a crew cracking a sewer line in the wrong spot, and water mitigation workers placing original artwork on a wet floor
redFlags: Recurring upsell pattern: at least 5 reviews independently describe a technician declaring major excavation or pipe replacement necessary, quoting $5,000–$15,000, followed by a second-opinion plumber finding either no serious problem or a much cheaper fix
793 BBB complaints in 3 years against an A+ rating is a severe contradiction — that volume of complaints for a plumber suggests systemic billing or service issues, not isolated incidents
Two reviews describe high-pressure contract signing during emergencies, with one reviewer explicitly stating they signed under duress at 12:30am with four employees present
At least two reviews allege supervisors misdiagnosed the actual problem location, performed unnecessary work, then quoted thousands more to fix the real issue
synthesis.emergencyNotes: Responsiveness is their most consistent genuine strength — multiple reviews confirm same-day or within-the-hour arrival, and one reviewer noted prior Thanksgiving Day service — but the fast response appears to be a vector for high-pressure upsells during vulnerable moments, so have a second plumber's number ready before you call.
synthesis.platformDiscrepancy: Google shows 4.8/5 across 3,099 reviews while Yelp shows 2.2/5 across 100 reviews, and BBB shows 793 complaints in 3 years despite an A+ rating — this three-way contradiction strongly suggests the Google rating does not reflect the experience of customers who encountered billing disputes or failed repairs.
