True provided us with answers and advice regarding our toilet issues presently and suggestions to avoid further issues in the future!! He was a great listener, had excellent communication skills and overall demeanor was extremely humanistic. As this was our very first time in calling upon the plumbing Dr for your issues we cannot be more appreciative with their outstanding service and professionalism!
Our sincere thanks!!!!
Samuel and Margaret Bozoian’s
Fairfax, VA

reviews.author: J Ses
reviews.text: Incredible work by Turé. Walked me through what needed to happen after a pipe burst. Did the work at a much more reasonable price than a competitor. Will be using Plumbing Dr. for all future plumbing needs!

reviews.author: Bridget Baiss
reviews.text:
Exceptional! Skilled, honest plumbing companies are hard to come by. Bill (the owner), Turé, Ken, and Lloyd were all outstanding to work with. They took the time to understand a very mysterious leak in our home that required multiple technologies, experience, and real problem-solving know-how.

They were amazingly clean, polite, communicative, professional, and genuinely ingenious in how they approached such a difficult issue. Their patience and thoroughness gave us complete confidence throughout the process.

I’m very grateful for their expertise and highly recommend The Plumbing Dr. to anyone in Northern VA who needs a skilled, reliable team.

reviews.author: Tyler Morson
reviews.text:
UPDATE: The technician who diagnosed my clogged kitchen sink drain was incorrect in their assessment. Upon further reflection, it's silly to think the technician could properly diagnose the issue considering they didn't even turn on the water. What ended up being a vapor lock caused by a clogged drain vent (diagnosed and fixed personally) was originally diagnosed as either a clogged drain pipe or improper drain design because of too sharp a turn in the piping. The MINIMUM estimate to fix what was improperly diagnosed was about $800-900 just to snake the drain. Other estimates for unnecessary work reached upwards of $2,500. Needless to say, I will not be using The Plumbing Dr again.

ORIGINAL POST: Very knowledgeable, and honest with their recommendations. I had an issue with my kitchen sink drain, and they assessed the issue, proposed solutions, and advised on potential alternatives. Not pushy in their sales either, which I appreciated.

reviews.author: Jacob Robie
reviews.text:
When I first purchased my house 1.5 years ago I asked The Plumbing Dr. to send someone out to make sure my sump pump system was in good shape. The plumber they sent said everything looked good, but it turns out there was no check valve installed or weep holes drilled which eventually caused a failure that dumped gallons of water into my basement.

It turns out these are pretty basic parts of a sump pump system that all installs should have, but because I trusted the tech they sent to know that I now have bigger problems. Instead of a simple fix I have hundreds of dollars in plumbing costs and water damage to repair.

reviews.author: Fran D.
reviews.text:
Adam from The Pipe Doctor was amazing.  As soon as he walked in the front door and I told him the bathtub faucet was leaking he said the cartridge in the shower handle needed to be cleaned.  He knew exactly what the problem was and was very patient with me while I asked about other possibilities I had found on Google (which obviously makes me an expert).  He just knew without a doubt what the problem was.  He said if he could just clean the cartridge the price would be about half the cost of replacing the cartridge with a new one.  I agreed to both options in case the new cartridge had somehow become damaged.

Once in the bathroom, he was surprised that the faucet handle was brand new, it had just been installed within the last month.  Another plumber had installed the shower handle the previous month, I called that plumber when water leaked through the ceiling below after a  shower a month later.  He couldn't find the cause so he just caulked around the chrome plate.  After he left it no longer leaked through the ceiling, but the faucet began a steady leak, that is when I called The Pipe Doctor.

Adam found the newly installed cartridge was clogged with pieces of what appeared to be pipe liner.  He pulled pieces out of the cartridge and then asked me to turn on the main water line for about 1 second to flush the line, I did this four times.  After each of the first 3  flushes, he pulled liner out of the pipe.  It ran clear after the fourth flush.  The pieces measure from 1/2 inch to 2.5 inches long.  He did not need to replace the cartridge as it had not been damaged.  He could not guarantee this had cleared all the material out of the lines. He said the problem was not due to something the last plumber did.  I did send that plumber an email just so he would know what to look for if another customer called with a leaking faucet.

This repair stopped the leaking faucet, but after a shower the next day the ceiling below again began to leak, so there was still material in the pipes that would need to be flushed out.

When Adam returned he said a possible source of this material would be the dip tube in the hot water heater, he wouldn't know until he installed a new hot water heater so he could take the old one apart.  I already knew it was about time to replace my 1998 hot water heater.  After replacing the hot water heater Adam found the dip tube in the old unit had deteriorated from almost 4 ft tall (the length of the hot water heater) to only 3.5 inches and what was left of it looked just like the material that had clogged my shower cartridge.  I got a very good price for the hot water heater and installation, plus the 15% senior discount made the cost more than reasonable.

Adam is a very upbeat, friendly, positive person.  He explained to me every step of the way what he was doing, why, and what he found, as well as the cause.  After I gave him his tip he told me any tips he receives are passed on to a good friend of Adam's, a clergyman, who uses the money to pay for medications for the elderly.

I had called The Pipe Doctor a number of times before each of Adam's visits.  Danielle was always friendly, courteous, and answered all my questions.  I would like to thank her for all her help and patience.

The Pipe Doctor is now my plumber, they are experts.

reviews.author: David G.
reviews.text:
My recommendation: Do NOT call The Pipe Doctor.  They were at my home in NVa recently to repair a small copper water pipe, broken due to the extreme freeze.  I called on a Tuesday evening, but received no call back until the following morning.  They arrived that Wednesday morning after 8:00 during regular business hours, and did resolve the problem, at least temporarily.  First, their website states they provide free estimates, but I later discovered they actually don't - and when a company starts out lying to you, it's obviously a bad sign.  Only one pipe had been damaged, but according to their plumbers, 2 pipes needed to be worked on because of their positioning; this seemed strange to me, but I accepted their assessment due to the need to get the job done and into work.  The pipes were located in an odd place, and from their description of the difficulty of the job, I expected it would take several hours, require special parts, tools, etc., so I also accepted their estimate of $600.  They finished in about an hour, with 45 minutes of time actually working on the repair, and did not re-fit the original copper pipes with new copper, but only applied some type of adaptor fittings and non-copper material.  The water did function properly afterwards, so I paid the fee and requested an itemized invoice.  I was told I'd be sent one by email, but the invoice I received did not provide any details on the parts, labor, additional charges for the service call and estimate, etc., and it was only upon receiving that invoice that I was informed there was no warranty on the job.  I emailed this company 12 (twelve) times for additional information and a detailed invoice, with no response whatsoever.  I later found what appear to be similar adaptor kits online for much less than $50; but even if both kits cost $50 each for a total of $100, that leaves $500 labor for a 45 minute job - over $500 an hour in labor costs alone.  

A similar issue on a different pipe occurred about 10 days later, and I of course did NOT call The Pipe doctor this time.  I called another local company (Kinnett), after-hours on a Saturday afternoon.  They returned the call, arrived and fixed the problem only a few hours later.  They replaced the original copper pipe with new copper, in an area that required outside work and access under the floor.  They responded more quickly, performed a much more extensive and difficult job on an after-hours emergency basis, provided all the billing details up front, and charged less than half the price of The Pipe Doctor.  Again - Do NOT call The Pipe Doctor for any type of plumbing job - you will likely be grossly overcharged for what is at best average work, and there are many, much better local alternatives.  D.G., NVa.

reviews.author: Coleen A.
reviews.text: Oh my, I'm absolutely shocked to see Gary responding to my initial review of 3 stars! Not only did I think he handled the whole situation poorly I'm now actually seeing that he's unable to be completely honest. I was sympathetic the loss of his grandfather, as I myself have just lost 2 son's in the last 5 year's. With that being said, all I said to Gary was you didn't leave any way of notifying your customers that you had a family emergency. Because he DID NOT tell me prior to leaving town. As a matter of fact he didn't even tell his own crew! Had he left someone to take calls, or even a message on his phone I'd have known! After reading my first review he called me and at first asked me to remove it. When I told him I would update it (which I thought I had) after the work was completed he demanded I take it down and even threatened not to come out and fix the mistake! At that point I will not be bullied or threatened and I told him that was up to him but the update would reflect that. His only saving grace in this matter was Lewis, who is the workmen that came out. I told Lewis that although I felt sorry for Gary's loss, his behavior was completely unacceptable and I would give them a update of only one additional star only because of his professionalism. Having owned my own small business, I do know that a simple phone message stating that you will not be available or due to a family emergency I will be out of town keeps your clients in the loop and your business running smoothly or if you have a trusted employee to run things while you're dealing with private matters. All this was preventable.

reviews.author: Kris Fizyta
reviews.text:
I hired The Plumbing Dr to replace a section of pipe connected to my bathtub. The work itself appears to be done well, and the team was professional on site. The quoted price was $1,190, but the final bill came to $1,531. While I was satisfied with the quality of the repair, I was not satisfied with how the final price was reached.
One minor gripe I have is regarding the cleanup of the job site. Because the pipe was located in my crawl space, the plumbers had to remove insulation to access it. When the job was finished, the insulation was left on the ground instead of being put back in place. It’s not a major issue, but it did feel a bit sloppy. It’s possible my expectations were off and most plumbers would not replace the insulation.
My bigger complaint was when it was time to pay. The mechanic informed me he needed to add a charge for snaking the line. He said the standard price was $391 but offered a discounted rate of $341. This was added to the original $1,190 estimate. I understand that unexpected issues can arise, but I believe I should have been notified before he did this work.
When I asked whether he felt the extra charge was fair, he said yes. I disagreed, but no sense in arguing about it.
Overall, the repair seems solid, but the lack of upfront communication about added costs left me disappointed. I had hoped to find my go‑to plumber, but based on this experience, The Plumbing Dr will be lower on my list for future work.

reviews.author: Miranda D.
reviews.text:
Shawn was awesome. The first time Gary came he was awesome, but after the first visit my voicemails went unanswered unless I called again. Gary was very unprofessional, he was rude and dismissive. I left him a voicemail asking for an earlier appointment date, when I didn't hear back I assumed the appointment was still on, it wasn't until I called him (30 minutes passed our appointment time) that he claimed to have left me several voicemails, and texts. Claims he called me several times without hearing from me. However during this time I got calls, voicemails, and texts from anyone else who attempted to reach me. He cancelled my appointment time all together. He continued to place the blame on me, even though in my voicemail I specifically said that if the earlier date couldn't be done then our original scheduled appointment would be fine. He just continued to tell me how I was wrong, and talked to me like I was an inconvenience, it was only after I asked him "what next" that he offered any resolution. 

If it weren't for Shawn, I would definitely have given a much worse review. Shawn deserves 5+ stars. Even after installation he followed up within an hour, as promised, and quickly came back when the water wasn't hot after an hour (gas gauge issue, not his fault). He was professional, and courteous. He was educated and informative. If I can work directly with Shawn every time then I will use them in the future.

reviews.author: Dandan L.
reviews.text:
I encountered a serious plumbing issue over the weekend and was fortunate to have Wendy from the Plumbing Dr assist me. She efficiently coordinated with and dispatched Harald, a skilled plumbing professional, to my condo. Wendy's thorough explanation over the phone prepared me for the process and potential problems.

Harald came in the morning and conducted a diagnosis and identified the main sewage problem, which required him to shut off the water and remove the toilet. However, the valve associated with the toilet was frozen due to age. Coordination with the management office to access the water main valve for my unit was then needed. Harald, unable to proceed without permission, temporarily left for another job.

Once I obtained clearance from the management office and informed Wendy, she promptly reconnected with Harald. He returned later in the evening, addressing issues with my toilet and bathtub and clearing the main pipe obstruction. I am very appreciative that this complex problem was resolved on a Sunday.

Harald is an organized, confident, and friendly professional, while Wendy is responsive, thorough, helpful, and organized in her coordination efforts. It is evident that they genuinely want to help me out during this challenging situation on a rainy weekend. I extend my gratitude for their outstanding service and will recommend the Plumbing Dr to anyone in need of plumbing assistance.

reviews.author: Al Iskander
reviews.text:
Simply OUTSTANDING !
My hot water heater blew a hole through its relief valve and was jetting a high pressure stream of water into the ceiling and flooding the lower level of the house.
First, telephone response within 1 hour, on an extended holiday weekend.  Two other plumbing services had been contacted... One never called back, the other responded two days later.
Second, dispatch of plumbers and arrival within 2 hours of the call on that same extended holiday weekend.
Third, immediately impressed with the bearing and professionalism of the responding plumbers.  They analyzed the problem and stopped the leak within minutes.
Fourth, having stabilized the situation, they gave a precise, clear, detailed explanation of the options for repair, and the exact price for each option.
Fifth, the work was done quickly and completely, all problems solved at the exact price offered.
In Summary:  I have never, in over 40 years of home ownership in different locations around the county, never, EVER found a better plumbing service than this.  In fact, nothing else comes close.  Finally, i wast gratefully amazed at the price, much, MUCH lower than what friends and relatives have been charged for similar service.

Don't even bother calling anyone else.  Call the Plumbing Doctor first.

reviews.author: Levert James
reviews.text:
Initially selected this company because their initial consultation fee seemed reasonable. The two plumbers arrived timely and conducted an initial assessment of the two toilets I need to have repaired both experiences the same issue. Then came the big surprise. I was told it would cost nearly $800 to fix two water fill valves because they had to turn the water off at the street blah blah blah. I was in the middle of a call so didn’t have much time to process the cost. So agreed to fix only one of the two. The job took less than 30 minutes which really made me wonder if I actually overpaid for the work.
Now here comes the kicker. I googled the fix then went to Lowes the following day and purchased a $15 water fill valve and fixed the second toilet myself in about 20 minutes and trust me when I say I’m no repairman, which is why I initially made the phone call.
I realize the repairman is under no obligation to do so but i would have felt much better about the experience if he had advised me that this was probably something i could have done myself.
So yeah, i definitely feel like I over paid and will definitely NEVER  use this particular company again. Even though it was an expensive lesson i now know how to do this work myself

reviews.author: Michael Rinick
reviews.text:
Although I had previously used The Plumbing Dr and had excellent service, this service on 20 March 25 was extremely bad from the initial arrival to when I cancelled the service.  I spoke to Wendy on 19 Mar 25 and was assured the service people would provide me the service I wanted.  Drs Trey and Brandon arrived, and I showed them what I needed.  Dr Trey told me he would rebuild the entire tank (not what I asked him).  Both Drs went out to the truck and had lunch).  I called Wendy to express my displeasure, and she told me to give them a chance (FYI:  she didn't allow me to share my thoughts).

When they returned from their lunch, they went to the kitchen and told me they didn't have the spouts or faucet in the truck (Wendy told me this morning that they had all parts in the truck).  Dr Trey then pulled out a form which showed all the estimates with the lowest being higher than $800.  At that moment, I cancelled the entire call.  I assure the plumbing company that I will NEVER call them for plumbing work again.

reviews.author: Robert Smith
reviews.text:
Outstanding service from start to finish!

From the moment I called, the experience was professional, friendly, and efficient. The staff answered right away, listened carefully to what I needed, and scheduled an appointment that worked perfectly with my schedule. The plumber arrived on time, introduced himself politely, and explained exactly what needed to be done before starting the job.

The work itself was done quickly, neatly, and with great attention to detail. They respected my home, cleaned up completely when finished, and made sure I understood everything before leaving. Pricing was fair and transparent — no hidden fees, no surprises, and worth every penny for the quality of work provided.

It’s rare to find a company these days that genuinely cares about their customers, but this team really stands out. I highly recommend them to anyone looking for reliable, honest, and skilled plumbers who take pride in what they do. I’ll definitely be using them again for any future plumbing needs.

synthesis.summary: Fast emergency response — proven on Christmas, Thanksgiving, and after-hours sump pump crises — but a handful of reviews flag diagnostic shortcuts that led to costly misdiagnoses and inflated estimates
strengths: Emergency availability is battle-tested: at least 5 reviews document same-day or sub-90-minute response on Christmas, Christmas Eve, and after 11pm for burst pipes and flooding
Technicians (especially Turé and Brian) consistently praised for explaining work, showing customers the problem, and discussing pricing before starting — mentioned in 6+ reviews

Complex problem-solving stands out: multiple reviews cite creative diagnosis of difficult leaks using multiple technologies, and one reviewer credits Harold with saving $1,500 by succeeding where another plumber gave up
weaknesses: Pricing transparency is inconsistent: one reviewer was charged $300 for a 5-minute screw-tightening after upselling attempts failed, and a 2018 reviewer felt the technician pushed unnecessary full-faucet replacement first

Diagnostic accuracy has failed at least twice in recent reviews: a 2023 reviewer discovered a missed sump pump check valve caused basement flooding, and a 2025 reviewer self-diagnosed a vapor lock after a $800–$2,500 misdiagnosis from a tech who never turned the water on
redFlags: Two reviews (2023, 2025) describe technicians missing basic diagnostic steps — one never turned on the water to assess a drain issue, another cleared a sump pump inspection without noting absent check valve or weep holes — suggesting inconsistent thoroughness across techs
One review alleges the owner threatened to withhold repair service after the customer refused to remove a negative review — a significant customer relations concern if accurate
synthesis.emergencyNotes: Strong emergency track record: documented responses on Christmas Day, Christmas Eve, Thanksgiving weekend, and after 11pm for a sump pump failure, with one reviewer reporting a licensed plumber arrived within 90 minutes; after-hours callout fee cited as under $100.
synthesis.platformDiscrepancy: Google sits at 4.7 across 358 reviews while Yelp shows 4.0 across 38 — a 0.7-star gap that likely reflects Yelp's smaller, more critical sample capturing some of the diagnostic and pricing complaints underrepresented in Google's larger pool.

plumbers.name: Cedar Park Plumbers
plumbers.address: 11300 W Parmer Ln #1021, Cedar Park, TX 78613, USA

reviews.author: Bianca Salazar
reviews.text: I was in need of an emergency plumbing company and they were the only one that picked up the phone. They even came on a weekend. Thumbs up

reviews.author: Melu Tava
reviews.text: They are the best plumbers in Cedar Park. They know their craft and have great prices

reviews.author: martin loroima
reviews.text:
I own a rental house in Cedar Park and I had an emergency with a couple of projects that needed to be fixed ASAP. First, my water heater is in the attic and my tenant informed me that there was no hot water in the whole house. The second problem was that when the tenant flushed the toilet there was water backing up to the bathtub. He tried to use the plunger to see if he could get the toilet unclogged but after spending almost an hour trying to unclog it he finally gave up.

All this happened over the weekend and I was out of town. I needed a plumber ASAP cause the tenant had some visitors and he was already frustrated. After calling multiple plumbing companies in the area nobody was available or they simply did not pick up the phone.

Finally, I found Cedar Park Plumbers and I was surprised they picked up the phone at 8pm on a Saturday. I explained what was going on and within 30 minutes they sent a plumber out to my property. He took pictures of the water heater and sent them to me explaining that it was an old unit and needed to be replaced. My water heater has an expansion tank and he gave me a detailed explanation of why I needed another expansion tank.

After that, he ran a camera to find the problem of the clogged line and found some tree roots in the sewer line. The toilet paper could not go through and got stuck causing the clog. He read his machine to remove the roots and unclogged the line. He told me that that was a temporary solution but once you have roots in the pipe they will grow again to the point where they can brake the pipe much worse.

Anyways, he had a brand new water heater and also installed it and the same night he fixed the 2 problems that were causing stress. I’m very very grateful to Cedar Park Plumbers for their availability and for helping me solve these 2 problems. I highly recommend them.

reviews.author: Gary Griffin
reviews.text: I scheduled an appointment with this company almost a week prior to the date they were suppose to arrive. The service was to fix a leaky toilet. This was for a rental property. My tenant agreed to take off from work to meet the plumbers there. On the scheduled date and time, no one arrived. About an hour after the scheduled time, I called, and after several attempts I got in touch with them. Excuses were given as to why they could not make it. Very unprofessional in my opinion. A phone call to reschedule would have been appropriate in this situation. If you schedule an appointment with someone, and they are waiting at a location for you, keep your appointments, or at least have the courtesy to call and let us know you cannot make it.

reviews.author: Jacob Troy
reviews.text: Needed a pretty important fix for a pressure release valve that was leaking in my front yard. The leak was bad enough that it was making my front yard muddy. Scheduled an appointment with a technician and they blew me off. No show, no response to my texts.

reviews.author: RAHIM MOMIN
reviews.text: I found this company on google to flush my tankless water heater. I reached out and they connected me to a plumber. One of the men came to our house and brought another employee too. The main person took the payment and left the employee to do the work. I asked for an invoice and he didn’t give me anything at all. The employee who was left to do the work was inexperienced. The employee “did his job” and left. I don’t know anything about flushing the water heater so I was trusting these guys to do the work right. After the employee left, half of my house was not getting hot water anymore. I tried to contact the main guy who didn’t answer until the next day. I figured out that the employee had turned off a switch and didn’t turn it back on. I fixed that myself as it was simple enough. The employee also ended up leaving the pipes leaking on two sides of our house causing dripping and leakage in the walls and into my house. I found water all over my garage floor and in my living room seeping in from where the water heaters are located. The leaking water caused damage to the floorboards. I messaged the main guy again to have him check the water heaters to make sure nothing else was messed up. He came to our house and instead of checking the problem he got upset that I was pointing out what was wrong. He did not check anything and stormed off. I haven’t been able to reach anyone at the company or the people who actually came to do the work. Disappointed in the quality of service. I hired people because I didn’t know how to do the job myself, but they left me with more work to do and caused damage.

reviews.author: Maria Melendez
reviews.text:
Ivran was great. He was very friendly and respectful and shared with us a lot of good information. I'm very meticulous about any person I hire to help take care of my house. I ask a lot of questions to see if they explain in great detail what they going to do to fix the problem,

I also value punctuality and responsiveness. The next tine I call this plumbing company I will ask for Ivran to be the technician assigned to my house. The problem we had was a leaking pipe in the kitchen sink. He gave us a couple options for how to best fix the leak. He explained which one he thought was the best way to go about it but let us make the decision. When we decided which option we’d prefer, he was quick, and got to work promptly.

He fixed it in an hour. Besides fixing the plumbing issue, he helped us connect a dishwasher that was also causing problems. That was not part of the repair we called for but he helped us anyway. Overall, we're pleased, and would recommend this plumbing company to anyone in Cedar Park or Leander.

reviews.author: Heberth Otero
reviews.text: They were prompt to assist us. We are an old couple. We've been in Cedar Park only for a couple of years. We still don't know many trusted plumbing companies in the city. My grand daughter was searching online for a recommended plumber and a few of her friends on Facebook recommended Cedar Park Plumbers. She gave us the number and they responded quickly. Once Ivran, the technician, arrived he inspected the water heater leak and notice of the supply lines had a small hole where the water was coming out. The fix was to replace the supply line but in order to to that he had to flush the unit. The problem was that the water heater was old and already had some calcium builtup so it him a while to unclog the section where the built-up was. When he fixed that he was able to flush the unit quickly. He had the part in this truck so replacing it was easy as well. He finally got fixed and replaced and the price I think was good. I was expecting to be more expensive but overall great company. I highly recommend it

reviews.author: Lisa Hammann
reviews.text: Called this company when I discovered I had water leaking through my walls from my water heater. They came out to see what was happening within the hour on a Sunday, and were able to stop the leak immediately, then come back within 48 hours to do a complete repair! Mike was the plumber who came to help me both times, and he was incredibly patient with me as I asked a million questions. He was very informative and made sure I stayed informed throughout the entire process. He even noticed a very minor unrelated issue that was also happening and was able to come back within the week to help me with that. Can't recommend them enough, I will definitely be going back to this company if I ever need more plumbing services!!

reviews.author: Draco Mons
reviews.text: They are amazing! They went above and beyond. I had a water leak from the garbage disposal. I called them but I did not have money to pay them. I told them about my situation. I have a daughter with special needs and I take care of her. I asked them if I can pay them with cookies. The technician thought I was kidding but then he realized I was being serious and acceded of helping me with the garbage disposal leak. I really needed help and they were kind enough to help me in this difficult situation. If I could I would give them 10 star rating. If you need a honest and kind plumbing company give them a call, they are nice people

reviews.author: Shirley Torres-Pena
reviews.text: This morning when I woke up I noticed water in the bathroom floor. I thought I forgot to close the shower curtains. After 30 minutes of drying up and cleaning there were water all over the floor again. That happened a couple of times again until I realized it was coming from the toilet. I called several plumbing companies in Cedar Park and Mike answered the phone and was able to squeezes me in his schedule the same day. He came, assessed the situation and the next day he replaced my old toilet. I'm impressed with how responsive they were. I'm pleased with their service.

reviews.author: Christina Torres
reviews.text: We had a shower issue and I called several places. Another company was able to get us in (just happened to be the first one I called) but I would absolutely call Cedar Park Plumbers next time as my first option. I spoke with Ivan, the plumber and he was very professional, transparent, and working to get to us quickly. His estimations were very manageable. I will keep their number for future issues. Their pricing is also really good. If it weren't for the timing which was really just luck of the draw, I would have opted to go with them.

reviews.author: Marco Maldo
reviews.text: I’m very pleased with the work Mike did. I called Cedar Park Plumbers to get an estimate on replacing my garbage disposal. You can tell the level of professionalism they have just by talking to Maria. She was very courteous and helped me make an appointment. John was the technician that came to my house. He was knowledgeable, very professional, and the price was affordable. My new garbage disposal was installed in a couple of hours. I will recommend them to my neighbors in Cedar Park. Thanks for helping me with my plumbing issue!

reviews.author: Armando Gomez
reviews.text: Cedar Park Plumbers has a good team of technicians. They rescued us from having a flood in my house. Suddenly, a pipe broke and the kitchen floor had water all over. I called them and they find the pipe that was broken. It was related to the washer which is inside the house. They tracked down the pipe that had a hole and replaced it with a new kind of material. It’s not PVC or copper, it’s something a little more flexible. Anyway, thanks again for helping us solve this issue. They’re very professional, I will use them again.

reviews.author: XMan
reviews.text: I live in Avery Ranch and was in a bad way on a Saturday. My water heater was leaking. Badly. Edwin and crew came out within a couple of hours and installed a new water heater-they picked it up from Home Depot for me also. I can’t say enough good things about these guys. They took the old heater away and cleaned up. Thank you to Edwin!! Update: My insurance company needed some documentation and Edwin was so nice about it and helped me with Allstates requests. Thanks again, Edwin!

synthesis.summary: The go-to for weekend and late-night emergencies in Cedar Park — they consistently answer when nobody else does, though one documented no-show raises a small reliability flag.
strengths: Weekend and after-hours availability is a standout pattern: at least 6 reviewers explicitly say Cedar Park Plumbers answered when all other companies didn't pick up or weren't available
Fast on-site response repeatedly cited — multiple reviewers report arrival within 1-2 hours of calling, including evenings and Sundays
Transparent communication during jobs: reviewers mention photos sent remotely, detailed explanations of options, and proactive identification of unrelated issues
weaknesses: One reviewer (4 stars) noted pricing felt 'a little high' relative to service quality, suggesting rates aren't universally seen as bargain-level despite the high pricing_fairness score

Communication score (77) is the weakest dimension, and the one negative review supports this — a no-show with no proactive call to reschedule points to inconsistent office-level communication versus strong on-site communication
redFlags: 1 of 75 reviews describes a clear no-show: appointment scheduled a week in advance, tenant took off work, plumbers didn't arrive and gave excuses only after the customer called an hour past the scheduled time — no proactive outreach was made

plumbers.address: 1616 Williams Dr Suite 101, Georgetown, TX 78628, USA

reviews.author: William
reviews.text: We had an emergency plumbing issue with no hot water with relatives coming to visit right before Christmas. Reliant put us on the schedule for the same day and determined that our 20yr old water heater was heavily calcified and needed replacement. Roman arrived in the late afternoon and worked hard for a few hours to uninstall our old unit and install a new 50gallon unit, replacing all the old fixtures and piping. He was detailed and thorough in walking us through the installation steps and even took a quick look at a few minor leaks in our house to make sure we didn't have any quiet money-sucking water leaks. Our hot water is back just in time for our holiday visitors.

reviews.author: Amber Thorp
reviews.text: Alan and Patrick arrived within two hours of us calling for an emergency with our sewer line on a Sunday.  They were quick, professional, and transparent about pricing. Would highly recommend Riliant and their team!

reviews.author: Randy Knightner
reviews.text: Allen came out Lowry short notice on a Tuesday and helped immensely with a broken water heater issue that my family had. He was incredibly polite and professional and solidified my want to use this company if further issues arise.

reviews.author: Anita T
reviews.text:
AVOID THIS COMPANY!!!

I want to give 0 stars but it makes me give 1 minimum  I paid a very high fee for an emergency repair.  The quality of the work was good, but after taking my credit card #, they asked my husband for payment and he gave them a check.  Then they proceeded to also charge my credit card twice TRIPLE charging us.  They notified me of the error, and said they would reverse the credit card charges but did not.  After over a DOZEN phone calls that were not returned, I finally gave up and contacted my credit card company who was able to reverse the charges.  I have never had anything like this happen in my decades of home ownership and I cannot emphasize enough NOT TO DO BUSINESS WITH THIS COMPANY!!!!

reviews.author: Fredy Valdez
reviews.text: They overcharged me for services. They came to check for a gas leak in my house. I thought they would have some expensive intricate way to find my leak, but no, they just used a bike pump and a diaphragm gauge and didn't even find the leak. Barely 2 hours of "work" and they charged me once 750$ then an additional 160$ the next day. For what, I have no clue. I never even received a quote or an invoice, and when I was told someone would call me to discuss pricing, no one ever did. I have tried calling several times, but it always sends me to an AI operator. When I called with a different phone number, I was able to reach an actual person who simply said I would get a call back, which I never did. Please rethink doing business with this company, as they will essentially scam you for your money. I will personally ensure those around me AVOID this company.

reviews.author: Brian L.
reviews.text:
I called Reliant on 05.10.25 and scheduled an appointment for their 8:00 AM to Noon time slot to have a toilet supply line leak repaired. At around 10:00 AM a representative named Alan showed up. He said that I needed to install shut off valves at the street and a new toilet in addition to repairing the leaking toilet supply line. I said if we were going to replace the toilet that I wanted a toilet bidet in rather than a regular toilet. He gave me the price which was over 4k to all this work and said he would be back in an hour with the parts. After three hours I had not heard from anyone so I text the number provided. They called and said someone should be there between 3:30 PM and 5:30 PM. At 3:30 PM I got text that the technician was 19 miles away. An hour later I text back and questioned where the technician might as the map showing his location showed him in the same place he was the hour before when I got the text that he was on his way. At about 5:30 a different technician named Jorge showed up. He reviewed the work to be done and that was when I learned that Alan was "the salesman". As we discussed the work to be done, Jorge mentioned that they would have to come back to instal the toilet seat bidet in a few days. I explained I didn't want a toilet seat bidet. I wanted a toilet bidet in one. We agreed to not replace my toilet but do the other work. When he was done he called into his office in my presence to ask them to remove the toilet and toilet seat bidet. It was then I learned they had billed my card for the whole amount before they had even done the work. The office rep told him that Alan would call me Monday and they would work out the refund. I never heard from Alan or Reliant on Monday or Tuesday. On Wednesday AM I called and explained the this whole story the office again. They assured me a manager would call me back that day. I did not hear from Reliant or Alan at all that week. I called again on Saturday the 17th and explained the whole thing to Abby. Abby assured me that someone would call me Monday between 4:00 and 6:00 PM. I explained to Abby that whats she was telling me was the same thing I had heard previously and that I was not confident someone would call me. It's Tuesday the 20th and I have yet to receive any calls from Reliant Plumbing regarding this matter. They have not provided me a receipt for the work either. Each time Reliant has set an expectation they have failed to meet the expectation they set. From time of the appointment, to the work to be done, and  to a return call. Because they have failed t call me back or refund me for the work that was not done, I have disputed the charges. I would not recommend this organizations for plumbing work.

Post my review I received a call. During that call Allen said he would call me right back. That was approximately seven hours ago and I've yet to receive the call back.  05.21.25 7:57 PM

I've yet to hear back from Allen or Reliant and my credit card has yet to be refunded for the work. I have now disputed the charges in total because it is clear Reliant is not going to respond. 05.29.25 7:42 PM

It's June 12, 2021 at 7:28 AM and I am on the phone with them again. Still no resolution, no refund and the same story. All I can do is take a message and have someone get back to you. I've said I wont get off the phone until this is resolved. Now I'm hold.

reviews.author: Adam S.
reviews.text:
I referred a client to Reliant Plumbing as one of three options for a sewer inspection, and they ultimately chose Reliant. Based on their experience this morning, I will be removing Reliant from my list of recommended service providers. When I refer clients, I expect them to receive excellent service, and unfortunately, that was not the case.

When my client called to schedule a sewer scope inspection for a home purchase, they were not given a quote or even a price range--only a service fee. It wasn't until the plumber arrived on-site that they were informed the inspection would cost $535. To put this into perspective, the licensed TREC home inspector, who was already on-site conducting the whole home inspection, would have charged around $280 for the same sewer scope. There is no clear reason why Reliant's price was almost double the standard rate.

The first person to arrive was friendly enough, but it was unclear what their actual role was compared to the plumber who eventually did the work. They may have been a salesperson or foreman, but their purpose on-site wasn't made clear. The actual plumber who performed the sewer scope arrived with a device that did not have a charged battery, forcing them to wait for one. As a result, what should have been a straightforward inspection at 8:00 AM dragged on until 11:30 AM--a completely unnecessary delay.

When it came time to locate the exterior and interior clean-outs, the effort was minimal at best. The second exterior clean-out was found by my partner in seconds, yet the plumber barely searched for it. Inside the home, they made an even more half-hearted attempt to locate the clean-outs under the bathroom sinks. They were ready to leave after only scoping from the street to the house, ignoring the majority of the plumbing under the home. I had to push them to complete a more thorough inspection.

The final straw was the report. For $535, my client received a two-page PDF with pictures of the clean-out entrance--but no images or videos of the pipes themselves. There is no real documentation of the sewer condition, meaning my client has no actual evidence of what they paid for.

This experience was frustrating, unprofessional, and overpriced. The lack of transparency, delays, incomplete inspection, and inadequate reporting do not align with the level of service I expect when referring professionals. As a result, Reliant Plumbing will no longer be on my list of recommended service providers.

Update 1: It has now been over 48 hours, and despite multiple attempts to follow up through their hotline, we have not received any additional photos, videos, or a credit. The manager continues to call at different times but is never available when we return the call. He also does not provide a direct number, so we're forced to go through the answering service again and again, repeating the same process with no resolution.

Update 2: They finally promised to give our client a credit, but as of today, it has still not been received. We also have still not received a reply to any of our follow-up communications.

reviews.author: Jordan H.
reviews.text:
I will start by saying this was one of the worst service experiences I have had with any business in any industry. Here's what happened: 

My toilet was suddenly not flushing well this week. After clearing a few separate clogs with a plunger, I decided there must be a blockage and called Reliant to check it out. They scheduled service the very next day and a tech arrived on time. After running a camera through the sink (not the toilet), the tech informed me that I have valleys in the pipes running under my foundation. He explained these valleys cause standing water that disrupt the proper functioning of the plumbing system, and concluded that this was the most likely root cause of my flushing issue. 

When I asked if he should also check the toilet before recommending that I let Reliant dig under my house to address the valleys, he briefly acknowledged that I could have him snake ($500) or pull the toilet ($1,200) before explaining that if I didn't address the valleys quickly, the problem would get worse and end up costing me much more. 

When I asked if he could run the camera through the toilet instead of the sink to determine if snaking or pulling the toilet was necessary, he said the camera could not negotiate the sharp turns inside the toilet drain. He also discouraged the snake option because "it's not guaranteed to clear a blockage if there is one." At this point, I decided I was going to either investigate the problem further myself or call another plumber for a second opinion. (My plumbing system has had absolutely no issues in the 6 years that I've lived here and it seemed like something more acute than sagging pipes was probably at play). The tech said that was certainly an option, but insisted he write up a formal estimate before leaving. I agreed, assuming he would quote the snake and toilet removal options. Instead, he provided me an estimate to correct the valleys in the pipes. THE QUOTE WAS FOR $73K!

After he left, I pulled the toilet myself and found a pair of my son's eyeglasses lodged in the bottom. I bought a new wax ring from Home Depot ($10) and re-installed the toilet. It now works perfectly. Altogether, the repair cost me $10 and 2 hours of my time, including the trip to Home Depot. I'm certain Reliant could have done it in even less time. 

I don't doubt that I have valleys in my pipes. And at some point, I may need to address them. However, I think it's absurd that the tech would choose to focus entirely on a $73K solution without exhausting all other possibilities first. I would never trust this company to diagnose another plumbing issue and I strongly advise you to do the same.

reviews.author: Samer K.
reviews.text:
This very well may be the worst company of any kind in Austin. Max H, don't bother responding as you do to all other 1 star posts with your BS about sincere apologies. Your company is a legit scam.

My story: I have a 2-year old water heater that is functioning great, and decided would try to perform annual maintenance for once to extend the life of this one. I signed up for a water heater "flush" for $99. Daniel Gonzales comes out, hooks up a hose, drains it for 5 minutes, and leaves. I'm surprised as I've watched youtube videos on this, and saw then flushing water through (not only draining) and cleaning the anode rod of any corrosion / buildup. Well... not with Reliant, you don't get anything of actual value.

Ok whatever, I'm out $99 dollars and nothing happened. I move on.

The next day I notice the drip pan is starting to fill and wonder if there's a new leak somehow in my water heater. 2 weeks later, I notice water leaking all the way out my garage and onto the driveway... indeed there's a leak. We never had a leak or any issue prior to this absolute horsecrap service. Call Reliant, they are super disorganized between the office secretary and the actual plumbers. Mixed messages and no clarity on how this will be fixed. And Daniel calls me back and diagnoses the problem on the phone that "its definitely not anything that they did that could cause this." lol really?

I have an almost new water heater, in working condition. You come and fiddle with it, promptly beginning a NEW leak, and then you're able to tell over the phone that it's not related to the work you did? It couldn't be more obvious of a lie given you're willing to make that claim without actually seeing the water heater.

Anyway, we insist he comes back to fix it. He shows up eventually looks at it, claims its not his fault, and slaps us with a $1700 estimate to fix a bunch of stuff that ISNT BROKEN, not even related to the leak. My wife, god bless her, doesn't take this crap, and insists he fix the damn leak. He tightens the connection on top where the leak seems to be coming from and voila, no more leak.

I'm 98% certain this connection was loosened intentionally to drive more business and rack up charges. Now after reading all the reviews on Yelp I'm even more confident that is the case. I haven't come across a company as vile as this one. Stay away!!

And Max H, please don't dare respond here. Not interested in hearing you lie through your teeth again.

reviews.author: Christy Y.
reviews.text: Before calling these people read my review, and then keep on reading because my experience is not unique. These people are crooks. We called them because a bathtub on our second floor was leaking and coming through a light fixture in ceiling below. It was a weekend and our usual plumbers were not available. Not knowing exactly what the problem was we wanted to get someone out that day. They came and cut a giant hole in our ceiling and told us we needed repairs to copper piping. They also tried to sell us a water heater at a discount if we decided right then to do it and assured us it would fail any day. We declined the water heater but felt stuck with them because we paid $150 just for them to come out, so we didn't listen to the icky feeling the slimy salesman was giving us. He quoted $1600 to make progressive cuts into the drywall and make copper pipe repairs as needed, and said he'd need an $800 deposit. We paid the deposit and he left. Two other guys came shortly after, looked into the hole in the ceiling and asked if there was a tub just above. They went and looked at the tub and discovered that the only problem was missing sealant on a joint in the drain. They fixed it in 5 minutes. When asked about whether there would be a price adjustment because this was a very different job than was quoted to us they said someone would call us the following day to discuss. No one called. On Monday my husband received an invoice/agreement for $1135, and they charged our credit card for the difference without our permission. We did not give them permission to hold our credit card number, but on the "agreement" they emailed they had forged my husband's signature, and that agreement with the forged signature gave them permission. I called no less than 10 times and no one was ever available to talk to me and they would not return my calls. I started an email chain for a paper trail, filed a police report for the forged signatures and protested the charges with my credit card company. I also consulted an attorney because it was free through my legal plan at work. So far my credit card company has given my money back, and if Reliant somehow gets them to reverse that I have the attorney on standby to help. These people are infuriating. I cannot stress enough that you would be better off dealing with whatever plumbing issue you have yourself rather than calling them.

reviews.author: Teri B.
reviews.text:
Completely Irresponsible!

Reliant came out and installed a tankless water heater in our garage. They overcharged for the heater, and did give a small refund after I called them out.  The water heater failed inspection by the city of Lakeway because there wasn't a water catch installed in case of a leak.  It failed again when the installer cut the back of the tray off so he didn't have to install it around the plumbing. When this was relayed to the installer, he told us he had "gotten hot, and wasn't feeling good, so he did it that way to get it done."

When he installed it, he also set the gas setting on natural gas, versus what we have- propane- which burns at a different temperature.  That caused the heater to fail, and cause smoke damage to our house and nearly burnt the heater up.  By the grace of God, our house didn't burn down. 

To resolve the issue, they cleaned and painted the exterior of our house and the inside of the heater, but refused to replace the heater in spite of what looked like extensive burn damage.  

Shortly after that, the heater quit working again.  We had a different plumber come out this time, and they discovered that the unit was so damaged that it was leaking carbon monoxide into our garage. It was also improperly installed, with the ventilation pipes so close together that fresh air could not come in- just exhaust.  Again, that was a huge problem. 

We received a bill from the new plumber in the amount of $2,500.  Reliant did agree to the fact that they were responsible for the damage, and would refund the money. That was on February 19th.  Since then, they have given us the run around and do not return phone calls. I went to their office on March 1st in person, and a man who said his name was Evan, the sales manager, said he would get resolution.  He would not provide his last name and stated he didn't have a business card.  I never heard from him. 

We have been diligent in seeking resolution, attempting to speak with them on a very frequent basis.  

They state on their website that they do quality work with 100% satisfaction guaranteed.  DO NOT BELIEVE EITHER CLAIM!  Do not risk having them install an item that should be easy for a qualified plumber.

reviews.author: Debbie Turner
reviews.text:
Edited:  go to the BBB site and read customer reviews for this location. There are other recent complaints of highly inflated charges for unnecessary services

Shady!! I had a leak at the base of my toilet and a broken flange was the cause. A plumber/GM named Mack came out and preyed on my trust and naivete and quoted $1500 after using scare tactics. He stated the flange couldn't be removed from the top of the pipe because in his "15 years of experience" it would be best to replace the pipe and flange. This would entail cutting through the ceiling and having to replace drywall and then he took it a step further by saying there may even be remediation needed for water damage to the subfloor. Well I panicked and fell for it and agreed. After he left and I was waiting for the real plumber to come fix the toilet I calmed down and used my brain and did some research. There was no damage to the pipe and I researched the removal of the flange. I called Mack back and told him no to the big repair and when the plumber showed I explained to him what I wanted done. The flange came out with no problem. The plumber who came out named Jacob was a doll and did  a great job. It's a shame he works for such a dishonest group. There was absolutely no reason to quote such a high price and for completely unnecessary work. I am now the owner of $1000 plastic flange. I feel like an idiot for falling for this scam and I hope that this review will keep others from falling prey.

F/U after owner response on this review today: I attempted to contact to discuss this matter and was offered no information on how to contact the person in charge of the GM. I was only given an email that is monitored by customer service assistants and received a blanket response and a statement that they would send it for further follow up. If the company honestly wanted to provider customers the ability to speak with a manager was displeased it would be much easier to make contact. Highly doubt I will hear back. Also there was obviously no damage that he should’ve been worried about to my pipe seeing as how it was intact and the flooring above was intact. Just a scam quote and no ability to immediately follow up with anyone

reviews.author: Lynda R.
reviews.text: Reliant Plumbing= SCAM. If I could give negative stars I would. We have been trying to get a call back for over a week now. Here is what happened: We had a gurgling toilet downstairs so we called them and they said we had tree roots that had broken a pipe (this is the second time they have told us this by the way- to the tune of thousands of dollars last time, ~2 years ago). I'm not saying we didn't -  but I will say both times it's been a catastrophic diagnosis. Coincidental? Not sure. In any case, we starting talking price. This is when it turned into a used car negotiation. They quoted us $10.2K -  we said we would get a second opinion and suddenly, the price dropped to $9K IF we didn't get a second opinion and if we agreed to it right then. They also tried to find out who we were calling -- the supervisor told us he had worked at Abacus and Radiant... classic used car tactics - talk smack about competition. We asked for a couple of hours to discuss it and the "supervisor" had to go outside and call the owner who ultimately told us no, the deal was now or never. So, with Christmas 5 days away, we agreed, as they said their contractors could work over the weekend. Once we signed, suddenly they could not get the same workers because we had negotiated a lower price so they would not start until Monday Dec 23. Now, this is what we have been looking at since then. They said they ran into a lot of rock and suddenly it would be $15K. We said that is not what we agreed to and we needed to talk to the supervisor. We have tried to call 5+ times over the past 1.5 weeks and NO phone call back, radio silence. The receptionist even said, "yes we have logged several calls from you, I will make sure you get a call back"- and still so far, we are stonewalled. So now we have a gaping hole 3' deep under our foundation on the coldest day of the year with exposed pipe and a dead yard. Reliant Plumbing is closer to a used car scam than a legitimate plumber. I can tell you what, we will NEVER use them again and I encourage every neighbor in Steiner Ranch and Austin to reconsider giving them your business. We filed a complaint with the state board and with BBB.

reviews.author: Rachel S.
reviews.text:
I had a leaking bathroom sink that seemed like a minor fix. I saw some good reviews for this company and my partner made us an appointment with same day service. The service fee was $89 and gets waived after you accept further work. 

Ray Baker arrived as our technician. I showed him where the sink was leaking from and he explained that he thought the installation of the sink was bad, which I didn't necessarily disagree with. During his diagnostic of the leak, he loosened another area of the sink. After his diagnosis, which only took one or two minutes, he went to another area of my house with my partner to provide her with a quote. 

I stayed upstairs to assess whether or not the sink had been put together in a way where it'd be usable while we got together the money for the quote Ray was about to provide. 

I noticed the part he'd loosened was leaking and it hadn't previously leaked, so I went and asked if he could tighten it before he left. Ray responded and said, "No." There was awkward silence and I politely asked again, but this time he agreed. I mentioned that I just wanted it tightened in good faith, so that the sink was somewhat usable while we got together the money to make the permanent fix. I didn't think this was an unreasonable ask, considering we'd paid the $89 service fee that's not refundable. 

Once he started tightening the pipe on the sink, I again mentioned that I just wanted it tightened in good faith, to which he replied that he'd just get money from the next job and didn't need our business. I didn't know how to respond, so I just didn't say anything. During my silence, I noticed Ray getting progressively more hostile and upset. Unprovoked, he mentioned several times that the sink was broken and tightening it wouldn't fix anything, that we needed to pay the money for the quote to fix it. What confused me about this interaction is that I never once said I wouldn't want the permanent fix, nor did I deny the quote. 

I won't be using this company again due to Ray Baker's behavior.

reviews.author: Matthew S.
reviews.text:
I had an extremely frustrating experience with Reliant and would strongly caution others before using them.

I contracted their services on 2/3 for a drain cleaning and specifically followed up to request a camera inspection prior to the cleaning because the work was part of an insurance claim and required documentation. The dispatcher confirmed this request was added to my service notes.

I rearranged my entire day expecting their arrival by mid-afternoon, even rescheduling mold mitigation services to the following morning to accommodate them. However, I received no communication until 7 p.m., and when the technicians finally arrived, they did not have the camera equipment I explicitly requested. Since their next available appointment conflicted with the mitigation services I had already rescheduled, I had no choice but to send them away.

At that point, I requested a refund so I could move on to another contractor. What followed was an exhausting runaround:

* I called at least four times over the next week and was repeatedly told the "refund department" would call me, which never happened.
* After about a week, I was told a manager had to talk with me before processing the refund and that a call appointment was scheduled. That call never happened.
* Instead, the original plumber showed up at my house unexpectedly, saying he was sent there for reasons unknown but had approved my refund. Yet, no refund has been issued.

It has now been two weeks, and I still have not received my money back. When I called again, I was promised a manager would contact me within 10-20 minutes. That was four hours ago. On top of that, many calls are routed to an AI agent ("Sarah") rather than a real person, making it nearly impossible to resolve issues.

I cannot speak to the quality of their plumbing work because the service was never completed, but their operations and customer service are disorganized, unresponsive, and extremely frustrating. I simply want my refund processed.

Very disappointing experience.

synthesis.summary: Shows up fast for emergencies and some techs do solid work, but billing fraud, wildly inflated quotes, and an AI phone wall that buries complaints make this a dangerous call at 2am when you're vulnerable.
strengths: Multiple reviews confirm same-day or within-two-hour emergency response, including Sundays and holidays
Several named techs (Roman, Alan, Jose, Brett) receive specific praise for thoroughness, communication, and professionalism
At least 3 reviews mention transparent pricing and clear walkthrough of work completed
weaknesses: At least 5 reviews describe final charges dramatically exceeding quotes, including one case of triple-charging a credit card and another billed 150% of contract price with no explanation
Multiple reviewers report being quoted $1,800–$27,000 for jobs that competitors fixed for under $500, with at least two confirmed misdiagnoses leading to massively inflated repair scopes
redFlags: 3 reviews describe an AI phone system that screens calls and routes complaints to voicemail with no callback — one reviewer only reached a human by calling from a different number

2 reviews report technicians performing little to no actual diagnostic work before issuing large quotes, including one tech who 'didn't step foot in a bathroom' before quoting $11,000 for a misdiagnosed slab leak
2 reviews allege billing for parts or services never rendered, including parts listed on invoice that were never installed
Acknowledged overcharges in at least 3 reviews went unrefunded for weeks or required credit card disputes to resolve
synthesis.emergencyNotes: Genuine emergency response capability exists — several reviews confirm arrival within 2 hours on Sundays, holidays, and late nights — but the same emergency context appears to be when inflated pricing and high-pressure upselling are most aggressively deployed.
synthesis.platformDiscrepancy: Google shows 4.8 stars across 451 reviews while Yelp shows 2.2 stars across 100 reviews — a 2.6-star gap that strongly suggests the Google rating is not representative, with Yelp reviews consistently documenting billing fraud, unreturned calls, and diagnostic failures that Google reviews do not reflect.
