reviews.author: william skinner
reviews.text: David was great, I had ruptured sewage line gave me the location of the break did not push for a complete line replacement  . Had a team the hand dug for the repair much more clean than having have and excavator do it and lower risk of damage to other systems.

reviews.author: Trinh Mai
reviews.text: Clinton from Mr. Rooter was amazing. He was patient, respectful, and took the time to explain everything while helping my parents at their nail shop. He fixed the issue and made sure everything was working before leaving. We truly appreciate his professionalism and kindness. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Michael Dow
reviews.text:
I tried to take off my old outside faucet and completely smashed the old copper pipe. Therefore that means no running water!!
Tun did a fantastic job. The pipe repair and faucet work like a charm. Great quality work as well. I had my water back on in a couple of hours as well. Mr. Rooter is more expensive. However, they get the job done right and are great to call in emergencies. Thanks again, Tun!

reviews.author: Jooky D.
reviews.text: Called for an appointment and got one quickly. They would not provide a price even though the guy that came had a price book with fixed prices. $350 to run a camera through the drain.  Originally he told me that it would be $500 but I told him I wouldn't pay more than $300. So he said he would do the camera work for free. He ran a camera through the drain and showed me some roots. Told me that it would cost extra ($250) to remove toilet and snake out the the roots. At this point it seemed like a big ripoff and I told him I would handle the clog myself. Lesson learned: Don't call someone on a workday after you just got up and try to solve the problem while you're still sleepy. If you know a good plumber just call them and pay their hourly rate to figure out whats wrong first and then proceed.

reviews.author: Mike R.
reviews.text:
Before you hire this firm to do any digging in your main sewer line, they will quote you a price for just using their camera to determine the cause.
My previous plumber, said a camera use would have cost $125. This firm charged me $500. However since my plumber was not available I had to pay the $500 or have it included in the $3,600 for digging up the source of the blockage.
Looking back, I should have just paid the $500 and waited for my plumber who would have charged me $1,200 for the digging, thereby saving me $2,300.
If your blockage has cleared wait and get an estimate for the camera use and get an estimate for the digging. Also, don't get their recommendation of using American Water Damage. The manager came in and tore up the baseboard and carpet believing insurance would cover it all. DOES NOT WORK THAT WAY. INSURANCE REFUSED TO PAY FOR THE AMOUNT OF DAMAGE HE DID.

reviews.author: Vinod P.
reviews.text:
WARNING: LONG

I sent an inquiry on their website to have them come visit my home on 1/21/19 for a leaking sink. That appointment was confirmed on the phone 5 minutes after the inquiry, but no one showed on that day. It turns out that whoever scheduled my appointment set it for 1/21/20. I let it go and had them come that Wednesday instead (1/23/19). Idiocy, but fine. They did their inspection and provided the quote that I agreed to, and then they stated they would come back the next day to complete the work. The tech told when he diagnosed it that he could be there between 2-4 the next day. He said whatever his job was that morning wouldn't run over. I knew I couldn't after 4pm that day and told him as much. He ensured that the job wouldn't take 2 hours, which is why I was fine with scheduling it. The company told me afterwards that they aren't sure they can make scheduled appointment times because they don't know what a client's problem will be until they inspect it. True, but then maybe, just maybe, they should tell their techs not to tell clients a specific time if they themselves aren't sure they can make it. Obviously, he didn't make the specified time frame, and I was rescheduled again for the following Monday (1/28/19). The work was finally completed on that day and the technician told me I could use the sink immediately. Surprise, it continued to leak the next morning. I called AGAIN after that to have someone come back out and look at the repair, at which point I was told someone would come later that day. AGAIN, no one showed up. They called me at 5pm to tell me they weren't sure they could send someone that day. At least someone who wasn't the original technician that I for obvious reasons did not want to see. Stop telling clients times if you can't meet them. It is NOT difficult. 

At this point, after THREE no-shows (and 1.5 days of lost vacation time at work), I called Benjamin Franklin to fix the problem, which they did the next day. That technician told me the puddy wasn't even the issue; the pop assembly was replaced that correctly fixed the problem. They attempted to fix Rooter's puddy job and tightening everything, but it unfortunately didn't work. I let them go that route first before the assembly was inevitably replaced in hopes I didn't need to get the part, but they did state it was the likely outcome. The Benjamin Franklin tech even told me verbatim that the manner in which the puddy was applied by Mr. Rooter would cause me to replace the piping if there is further problem. Fantastic. A plumber who literally made your plumbing worse.

I also had them replace a fill valve on another toilet. The problem for that came back after a couple weeks as well. I ended up replacing that myself instead of calling for a warranty repair. I frankly wasn't sure anyone would come.

They said they would meet me "halfway" and give me $150 back. My bill was for $430. They can't even do math correctly. Halfway of a $430 bill that they essentially did nothing on isn't $150. What it essentially amounts to is that I called Rooter out to my house, was told an estimate, and declined it. Both "jobs" they performed were fixed by people other than them. Why call for warranty work when you don't know if they'll come, and then you have to take even more time off for someone who's given you ZERO indication you can trust or rely on them? I gave them one opportunity to fix it again when I really shouldn't have, and they still missed it. It isn't your job to accommodate a company continuously into your schedule without guaranty they will come. Not for something you are paying them for.

I literally provided the invoice/receipts in my complaint that reflects that I did in fact have the parts replaced/repaired after their work and they turned a blind eye. It was ALL there. How convenient for them to blatantly ignore everything since it explicitly shows how they misdiagnosed my issue. And they seriously still can't understand why I wouldn't want their shit company back in my home for warranty work? What's the point in calling for warranty work when they don't show up? How many chances is a company that's shown to be completely incompetent supposed to be given? They know if they were in my shoes that they wouldn't allow someone who's treated them the way they treated me and my time back into their home either. They didn't even try to address my (completely valid) points in my last response email. And I have all correspondence if anyone wants to read it to see. Apparently, they don't realize they're essentially admitting fault for it all but refusing to do the right thing? So now I will share it with anyone who wants to read it. 

DO NOT use these guys. You can't trust them as far as you can throw them. Give Benjamin Franklin a call and have your work done correctly and on time.

reviews.author: Lewisville L.
reviews.text:
Horrible Experience. At first, the interaction with the technician was great,  anyone could tell very quickly from having a conversation with him, that he was very knowledgable. I was dealing with a broken sewage pipe under a new patio I had just finished building and I knew that repairing this was going to be tricky. The Mr Rooter technician suggested that we cut a 3x3 space in the newly poured concrete so that he could get under the patio to do a spot repair. This technician first quoted me $3,900 to have the concrete cut, the hole dug and the spot repair completed. For all of that work, that price actually seemed to be fair. Since this was a very important matter (until this was to be fixed, we couldn't use two of our full bathrooms) I decided to make the deposit of just over $1,000 so we could get the work scheduled, this is what I was told we had to do in order to get a project started. Before beginning, I wanted to speak with my patio contractor to make sure everything would be okay. She was afraid that if we were to do that, some support might give out as there was a stone fire pit about 6 feet long right above where the spot fix needed to happen. After exploring other options of how to get around having to cut the concrete, we decided that it was really the only logical path to go down. This is where the issues and dishonesty of the company began to come alive.

Once I notified the technician that we would like to take the offer and began on the agreed upon project, he said he would have to now come back out and re-estimate the work. Very strange, right? When he shows up, he now says the work will not be $3,900 but, it will be closer to the mid $5,000 range. Keep in mind, at this point nothing has changed. This was very unsettling for multiple reasons, 1. This was clearly a rip-off tactic, 2. I had my contractor agree to cut the concrete for me, out of the $3,900 estimate I was given, this was a $1,099 line item cost. 3. They already had my over $1,000 deposit that I could not get back even though they hiked up the estimate substantially. But wait, It gets worse.

Once the diggers show up, they don't bring enough tarp to fully secure the patio area and they leave dirt and filth everywhere. That didn't bother me all that much. What bothered me is when they were scraping their shovels recklessly to fill the hole back in, they were dragging their shovels against new stone stairs, scratching them up very badly and causing damage (all because they did not put tarp down). When I confronted them and the Mr Rooter technician about it, the Mr Rooter technician became very defensive and argumentative. He began to walk around the backyard to areas far away from where the work was being done and began saying that there are cut marks all over the stone work in other places (absolutely not true). When I disagreed with him about that, he began with very sarcastic remarks, like "I cant bubble wrap the whole house". He then proceeded to tell me that he felt like me complaining about this "was a slap in the face" and that "he's been trying to help me". I'm sorry, in case I missed something, I am paying Mr Rooter to be here, this is not volunteer work. After our bad ending to the day he went to get the paperwork for completion and then began admitting that the diggers had done wrong and apologized and said that he uses them all the time and that they have never done anything like that before. Sounds like an admission of guilt to me.. I asked multiple times to speak with a supervisor, his answer to me was that since it was late and they were gone from the office, that someone he already spoke with would be calling me first thing in the morning. That was a lie. No one called. I have followed up with their office after filing a formal complaint and I still have not received a call. DO NOT EVER USE THIS COMPANY.

reviews.author: Maria A.
reviews.text:
As I sit here on a call with the "gentleman"  named Thomas who is handling inbound calls for Mr Rooter (after he hung up on me once before) 
He's telling me that if my intent is to file a complaint upon completion of work he wouldn't  be honoring the warranty from the horrid work Pasquale. 
There is a "60 Day Warranty" on their OUTRAGEOUSLY PRICED WORK.
We were charged a total of $675.00 for a drain clean out and a "camera" to be run which we were NEVER shown and footage off. When I mentioned "Could it be from flushable wipes..? He instantly saw a glimmer of hope and clung onto that as a cause! It was almost comedic when it happened how he lit up like "YES..this is how we get them" 
As a new home owner having a drain clean out service seemed like something almost normal. But the fact that work was done 3/10/2023 and we are now on 4/29 as it's happened again is wild. 
There are two people who live here and we don't make poor decisions when it comes to what is flushed and such. 
What's really interesting is when we asked Pasquale "Does the drain clean out lid need to be shut?" He insisted NO! I told him I'd never had one before being in apartments all my life and told him I was seeking guidance but he obviously knew what he was doing. Prepped up for the next clog. Left that sucker right open. Do yourself and favor and don't believe the fabricated reviews from their friends and family. Out of now 96 reviews we all know the fact that they are at 1 star speaks volumes. If I had come to Yelp before using their services I can assure you we would have never made this mistake so I hope we can save you from this nightmare!

To add insult to injury, after having Thomas hang up on me and attack me verbally he put me on a long hold and came back and offered to charge me 99.50 to come out tonight...leaving us NO CHOICE but to pay. This review I'm hoping saves you from this joke of a company. Call Mr Local Plumber and save yourself the headache.

Cut to 3 hours later and we spoke with Lewis "The Receptionist" who for 15 minutes tip toed around the fact that he said he works at a desk in a office building and just takes inbound calls and submits requests into a system. He had no record of my ever giving my credit card number to Thomas (so now I need a new card before Thomas does fraud on my account) and Lewis "the receptionist" still has no idea if the emergency call we made at 4:00 was ever made. In fact he found it comical he couldn't help me and eventually just put me on hold and never came back. 

Then we have Kevin call. (He works for an after hours company) 

Here's the TWIST...

So how Mr rooter works is they offer up to a 60 day guarantee on the work they provide (so they say) BUT ONLY AND I STRESS ONLY if the SAME person comes back to essentially further damage the first job he did. 
Kevin explained that even if we paid the $99.50 emergency charge he had to charge us in FULL in order to then submit for a reimbursement later. 

The ONLY and ONLY glimmer of hope in this is the fact that Kevin took initiative which NO ONE ELSE has (Thomas and Lewis ) and called his counterparts at work and they advised they would allow him to come and handle the issue and they would essentially take it up with Mr Rooter and Pasquale. 

This has been an absolute nightmare and I can't wait for it to be over.

reviews.author: Stuart B.
reviews.text:
I am not sure why others have given such bad reviews.  I can't say the prices are the best as I have nothing to compare them to.  But when I had my insurance adjuster out to see if they could help cover the cost, he said that for as much as they had to dig up he did not believe we were being overcharged.

With that said, a toilet was lifting up from the floor in our front bathroom and it would gurgle when water was run in other drains.  When the plumber came out they ran a camera though the outside access.  They saw roots in the pipes (they let me look) and the camera went under water more than twice.  

The drain pipes were ancient.  They were still made of concrete and were in poor shape.  Some were leaking under the foundation and there was quite a bit of waste water under our home.  The plumber, Donny, explained everything and did not sugar coat the cost.  They started work pretty much the next day and kept us informed of everything that was happening.  

They tried extremely hard for the repairs not to impede our daily lives and did a really good job.

Can I say I loved to pay what we paid to have the work complete?  No, I am not insane.  but the work needed to be done or it would eventually do more damage to the plumbing and the foundation.  I can't say that I wouldn't have charged as much or more for everything they did.  I saw some of the roots they pulled from beneath the house.  They were huge.  It took them about a total of 6 days to complete the work, but they strived to work around our schedule.

When we were concerned about an item, the plumber came back and took a look to ensure it was good to go even after the work was completed.  

They were nice and professional and I really don't have anything bad to say about them. 
 I would call them again if I need more work done.  I feel they will take care of me right THE FIRST TIME.  So many contractors here don't seem to care.  This one did.

On a final note I would give them 5 stars but can't really judge the price as I don't have anything to compare it to.  Other than that we have no complaints and were very satisfied.

reviews.author: Brandon L.
reviews.text:
Beware!  These "good reviews" are fake!  See their Yelp reviews and the Better Business Bureau before hiring these guys. They are a total scam!  It cost me approximately $1000 for them to basically come out and break my toilet.  

I called them on a Saturday evening as a toilet sewage was coming up from the drainage and going into the shower.  I talked to an answering service that said it would be $90 for the plumber to come out, however they would apply the $90 towards whatever needs to be done to correct the issue.  2 hours later, I get a call stating that the answering service was wrong and that it is approximately $180.  So, by that time it was too late and no other company was answering their phone. The plumber goes out to the property and calls me back after inspection and states to me that they don't get up on the roof for cleanouts as they needed to go thru the air stack to do the clean out. Therefore, he wanted to charge me $180 just to come out and tell me that.  He then gave me a different option that would cost more expensive of removing the toilet and cleaning out the drain for a total of $780 for an hour (additional fees if longer than an hour).  By that time, I had no option but to go with it because he was going to charge me $180 just to tell me that they didn't get up on the roof. 
Now get this, approximately 20 mins later, the plumber calls me back and states he broke my toilet and that he would credit me approximately $100 for breaking my toilet (which ended up costing me an additional $300 to replace and install a new one).  
Lastly, 3 days later, we start to have the same issues with the drain and had to call a different company to come out and do the job correctly. After the new company did the cleaning, I paid them to camera the drain to make sure that the only issue was a clogged pipe.  It came back that the issue was a clogged pipe and that Mr. Rooter did not fix the issue.  

So basically, it cost me almost $1,000 for Mr. Rooter to come out and break my toilet.  You have been warned!  This company is a complete scam!

reviews.author: Katie M.
reviews.text:
As many have said, zero stars would be the most appropriate rating. DO NOT EVER CALL THIS CON ARTIST PLUMBING COMPANY!!! I called with a clogged washing machine drain line. The tech showed up and saw the age of our house (late 50's vintage) and must have seen dollar signs. He immediately started talking about how these old houses have cast iron pipes and they can corrode and would need total replacement. He then got the camera out to look in our drain and saw a cast iron p-trap and immediately said it must have collapsed. He then used a drum auger to make two attempts at clearing the clogged drain. The auger was getting locked up and started twisting around. He showed me all this to make a point of showing me that this was failing and nothing could be done. He then went on to say that the sanitary line would then need to be up-sized to meet code requirements so we would need to do a total replacement of the sanitary line from the kitchen and laundry area. He then provided an estimate of $15,796.32 to do this work.
I did also point out the main clean-out near the street and the kitchen clean-out to the tech but he never opened either.

I had another plumber out the next day for a second opinion. They used a pistol auger and were able to make headway in the clog. They then opened the kitchen clean-out and snaked from that side as well. They even opened up the main clean-out to ensure there were not issues from that side.
With an hours worth of effort they were able to fully clean our line and leave us in better shape with our entire drain line with all of their effort. For two techs working this long they only charged me $175.

Their tech, however, after telling me the sky is falling when he put in 5 minutes of effort, charged me $286.17. 

I cannot help but feel scammed. I paid a ton of money for next to no work to then have him try to up sell me on SIXTEEN THOUSAND dollars worth of work. I am stunned by this charade.

reviews.author: Brad N.
reviews.text:
I don't like to leave negative reviews, but I will this time. Don't be confused by the bait and switch this particular outfit engaged in with me. I hired Mr Rooter to come out and assess the situation, a small leak in my main line. The individual who came out was nice and pleasant, but really didn't know how to assess or locate a very small leak in the line. In fact, it was stated that his company didn't even have equipment necessary to really do so. Despite that, he recommended somebody else coming out with more experience, but not a master plumber, to try to assess the situation. One hour was nearly $550. He originally wanted almost 1100 for an initial two hours, which I did not feel comfortable paying for. I told him to figure it out in one.

Unfortunately for me, my house is very unique and I think they bidded their subsequent so-called and insane repair bid at $21,500 based on the appearance of what I can afford. I will NEVER recommend this company. In fact, I will suggest people not to hire them for anything. They should be ashamed of themselves. They should get back to honest billing if they want to survive. If not, they should be shut down permanently.

For the $550 bill, it was $250 per hour for the one who didn't know what he was doing and $350 per hour for the other one. A master plumber doesn't even charge that. But out of desperation, virtually, everybody is willing to pay whatever it takes to get the repair analyzed and hopefully done. Hopefully everybody else will read this review before ever considering this company.

Be aware. And don't be taken like I was. I have already enlisted the services of a master plumber who I anticipate his total aggregate fees being only around $500-$1000, not $21,500. And I will update with what his total bill is once he completes the job tomorrow

reviews.author: Steve H.
reviews.text:
I only wish I had come to this page before. Mr. Rooter does not care about repeat business. They are expensive and the owner/managers only care about the short-term buck. You just need to look at their Facebook page--it is all from Mr. Rooter, or customers who have had a bad experience.

A Mr. rooter plumber came to my house to clear my kitchen drain. There were two problems that day:
1. The snake machine Mr. Rooter supplied was broken so the technician had to use a smaller drill version which could NOT clear the drain. In the process, he used this "work-around" tool and snaked towards the kitchen breaking my u-bend pipe.  I did not recognize this issue for a couple of days.

2. He fixed the proper clean-out tool on my front porch but got a lot of grease spots on the concrete. I actually felt sorry for the plumber, his company sends him out with faulty equipment and he has to fix it. He got the drain cleared and I paid the appalling sum of $275 for the service. (I agreed to it but it was late friday afternoon and I had little choice.)

So Sunday when I am doing dishes I realize water is pouring out the sink from the u-bend. This was OBVIOUS how it was damaged. This $2.77 part was never meant to be snaked with a tool of this type. You can see how it scraped through the part and cracked it at he bend. Moreover--this was NOT the problem area.

I understand that things can go wrong--grease and breakage--but when I called this morning, the dispatcher explained to me that nothing they use could have broken that part and that he'd be happy to send someone out, but that they'd most likely have to charge me. When I asked for a referral of a product that I could use to get the grease off of my patio--he hung up on me!!  Can you believe it? DO NOT HIRE THIS COMPANY!

reviews.author: Sherry D.
reviews.text:
I had the best experience with Mr. Rooter.  I woke up Easter morning and came downstairs to my dining room and kitchen 
  flooded.  I called Mr. Rooter and they said someone would be out 11:15 am.  At 10:55 am, Ian Ontiberoz, with Mr. Rooter showed up.  He was absolutely fantastic!  He immediately turned the water off so no more water would leak.  He located where the leak was coming from.  He determined it was the hot water pipe because the water was hot from the leak.  So  he turned the water back on but shut the hot water off so I would at least have water.  He called restoration team for me so they could get the water cleaned up and getting fans going.  The restoration team was there within an hour. The cleaned up the water and got the fans and dehumidifier going.  At least that put my mind at ease.  The next day, Ian was there first thing in the morning with another technician, David Couder.  They determined that the leak was coming from under the slab.  They said instead of tearing up my kitchen floor, they would have an excavator come out and dig a tunnel outside under the slab.  David and Ian were so great with communication  Both were always keeping me up to date of what was going to happen and what was going on.  This was a very frustrating situation and Ian and David made it less stressful for me.  I couldn't ask for better service.  Ian and David were so knowledgeable and very easy to talk with.  They fixed the leak.  Both of them were here everyday till the leak was fixed.  Ian and David did a fantastic job and because of these two, I will be using Mr. Rooter from now on and requesting these two.  I couldn't ask for better service than from Ian and David.  Thank you so much Ian and David.

reviews.author: Jonathan F.
reviews.text:
Customers Beware!!!!  PLEASE LEARN FROM OUR MISTAKE!!!!  Do not do business with this company!!!!!

On a Friday morning, my wife called Mr. Rooter to fix a clogged drain in our laundry area.  (She called our "regular" plumber first, but he was too busy.  Because we were hosting out-of-town guests that weekend, he reminded her that a simple de-clogging could be handled by one of the "drain rooter" companies.  Boy, did we learn our lesson!!!) 

 Mr. Rooter's employee showed up, quickly looked at the drain,  and said that the drain pipe was definitely clogged. He used the drain snake (auger) to unclog and was finished in about 15 minutes--a VERY routine plumbing procedure.  As he was packing up his equipment, I arrived and met him in our kitchen where he presented the bill:  It was for $550.17!!!!!!!!

Needless to say, we could NOT believe it!!  We asked him about the outrageous costs, and he gave us a very incoherent and doubtful explanation--said it took "special equipment," the flat-rate pricing is set by his company, etc.  So, we asked him to confirm the price with the central office/dispatcher.  He became angry and very belligerent at that point, and said there was no use talking with the dispatcher because HE (the apprentice plumber) was the owner and she worked for him!!!!  (Obviously, not true.)   At that point, we tried to keep him calm, but we felt very threatened by his aggressive gestures/language.  This "negotiation" continued for almost 30 minutes.  We finally called Arlington PD because we were concerned for our safety.  They told us to go ahead and make payment (via phone) and then dispute the charges later which we will definitely do!!!

plumbers.address: 7800 W Jewell Ave Unit G, Lakewood, CO 80227, USA

reviews.author: Anne Marie Disney
reviews.text: Dakota was great. Very efficient and kind and walked me through everything giving good suggestions. Very knowledgeable

reviews.author: Ben Hale
reviews.text: We had sewage backing up into our basement shower and overflow drain in our HVAC room. We called Roto Rooter and they were able to send someone out within one hour of calling. The tech, Dakota, was great! He was very knowledgeable and willing to explain everything that he was going to do. He spent several hours at our house making sure he thoroughly cleaned out our sewer pipes. A supervisor, Mike, also came and did a free video walk through of our pipes to help identify other problem areas. Dakota even came back a couple days later to fix a small leak in our clean out access point. I would highly recommend them!

reviews.author: Mile High Shade
reviews.text: We noticed last night that our downstairs toilet was starting to leak around the base and so we immediately looked into getting someone out to take a look. Booking the appointment was quick and easy, and Stephan showed up exactly on time the next morning ready to help us out. He was open with his communication, letting us know there were a few options that might work and helping us choose where we wanted to start. When the first option didn’t fix the problem, he was upfront and honest with next steps. We chose to do a full main drain snake and he got it done promptly and efficiently! He explained his process and what the problem was afterwards so we knew what to look out for in the future! All in all a great experience and we highly recommend Roto-Rooter and especially Stephan for any drain and plumbing needs

reviews.author: PHIL R.
reviews.text: They refused to give me a ballpark price on a clogged kitchen drain over the phone. When the plumber arrived he quoted me a live near $400. I sent him away.

reviews.author: Randy F.
reviews.text: I had a leak in a pipe that was on recall. They quoted me 4800 for full pipe remediations (which is a huge job). The other estimates i had gotten were twice that. THey assured me after deep questioning that they could handle it and be done in 8 hours. They had almost no material to use, no drop cloths . They dint cover the AC intakes so dust was pumped all over the house. Drywall dust pointless all over the hardwood and my furniture. Instead of removing sheets of drywall they just cut little hole after little hole. They had to come back 3 times, once for a leak in the new pipe,once to hook up a forgotten refrigerator line and again to hook up another line they forgot. ON the last one i had to cut a new hole in the drywall i just replaced. 4 days, 56 holes and a massive mess. THey guys were nice, just not at all prepared for a project of this size. Yes, the fine print says we don't move furniture.  That is fair enough but they had told me 5 holes in the drywall, not 50.  I called a "manager" and he said he'd give me 1k off. Then he said " we had to charge you $$$ money because of al the extra time it took". He'd said hew as actually doing me a favor. It was incredibly insulting. I turne up the noise level and got another manager and he did reduce the original cost by 1k.  Then the 3rd visit and they cut a hole in the cieling i had just paid 5k to repair. They said they'd get me chalk for that repair but i have yet to see it. I think these guys are pressed to upswell to these big jobs and they just don't have project management capability. They are also big enough to absorb the loss if it turns south. They are responsive to short notice requests and their switchboard is superb, but this....was a mess.

reviews.author: Ryan G.
reviews.text:
We called Roto-Rooter 11/10/2013 (on a Sunday) as our basement drain was backing up. We called the dispatch department around 11:30 a.m. and were advised someone would be out within 2-hours and we would be notified 30 minutes prior to their arrival. Dispatch called again around 12:45 advising there was a delay and they would notify us when the next plumber was available. They called about 10 minutes later advising someone would be to our house in 30-45 minutes. Within 30 minutes we had a plumber at our house.

The communication up front was excellent and the expectations of when someone would be out were also exceptional.

When the plumber arrived he was friendly, courteous, and promptly proceeded to troubleshoot the issue. He advised he would need to snake the drain, and advised up front what the charges were to do so. He asked for a signature at that time to confirm it was okay for him to proceed with that work. He worked on snaking the main drain line for a few hours and indicated the work was completed. We tested by flushing some toilets and there were no backups indicated. Paperwork was finalized and we issued payment for the charges incurred. These were known charges for snaking the line, plus we purchased a bottle of drain cleaner. No other charges were incurred.

About 10 minutes after he left we ran our washing machine and the drain began to backup again. We immediately called Roto-Rooter and he was sent back to address. He attempted to snake the line again with no success so he advised he was going to remove the toilet to attempt to snake through that line. There was no indication at this time there would be any additional charges to remove the toilet. 

The plumber worked on the line for several additional hours with no luck so he called another plumber to come and assist with the problem. The other plumber was traveling from Parker, up to our home in Arvada and arrived approximately an hour later, close to 8 p.m. The first plumber indicated he was more of a true plumber and could repair and replace our pipes, but this other plumber was a line cleaner and knew what he was doing. 

When the second plumber arrived he brought a second drain snake machine. After snaking the line for a while the second plumber advised the first plumber's equipment was faulty and not working properly so he was unable to clean the line. Around 9:30 p.m. they completed their work, the line was clean and water was flowing freely with no backup issues.

At this time the second plumber advised he recommended we send a camera line down our drain to determine if there were any other issues and this would charge an additional $150. We refused this additional service as the lines were flowing freely. We were then advised by the first plumber that there were going to be additional charges to remove the toilet and to snake the line further out. There was no indication of these additional charges until after the work was done, which was clearly a different approach from when the first plumber arrived, advised of service to be done and associated charges.

We sat down with the plumber to go over the charges and they had almost tripled from our first payment this morning with essentially no other services provided, outside of their time. 

The charge to remove the toilet was higher than the charge to snake the drain, which seems odd, but if we had known there was nearly a $300 charge to remove the toilet, we would have removed and reset it ourselves.

Additionally, this does not appear to have been necessary as the second plumber who arrived was able to successfully snake the line with his equipment and it appears the first plumber was less experienced in this aspect of the job.

Both plumbers were friendly and courteous, but the lack of explanation on additional charges was beyond frustrating. The plumber reduced our bill as he could see our frustration, but it was still $200 more than the original bill we paid earlier in the day, with no real reason for the same. 

We hired Roto-Rooter because of their longstanding reputation in the industry. If we wanted to hire a plumber who was going to come in and not explained the process of work and any charges we may incur we could have surely elected one of thousands of plumbers in the Denver Metro area to meet these needs, but we wanted a company that would charge us reasonably amounts and explain to us what charges we may incur prior to doing the work. 

The only reason there was a two-star rating was because of the communication from dispatch and the friendly approach of the plumbers. 

Bottom line, we had plumbers in our home for around 8 hours on a Sunday, when it seems if the work would have been done appropriately the first time the work should have taken around an hour (according to the second plumber).

reviews.author: Deanna C.
reviews.text:
Roto Rooter gave me an estimate of $5500 for water mitigation after my basement bedroom, laundry room and partial living room were backed up with sewage.  At the end of it all they are charging me $8200, which had I known the flaws and inconsistency the techs would leave me to take care of, I would have NEVER hired Roto-rooter in a time of need.

Summary of issues. 
The technicians only removed one 8 foot stretch of drywall (not the wall that was majorly affected/outside of laundry room), which was insufficient due to the damage that we explained to the techs. We had told Brian the backup happened on a Wednesday night, where as they did not come and perform the work until later on that week Saturday. After we expressed that the "sales guy" took water readings and showed us all of the saturated walls, the technicians STILL did not listen to us and did not take out the walls.  

The technicians told us they would take out 24 inches (2 feet) of drywall.... They only took out 23 inches, my husband had to correct their faulty measurements by cutting out 1 inch of drywall.

Brian and Robert from Roto Rooter did not connect the washers to the washer and dryer.... found out the hard way after doing a load in the wash, the laundry room floor had water coming from under the washer and dryer.  The washers to the Hot and cold hoses were Missing, we found them on the basement floor........ Had to buy new washers because of their incompetence, my husband took care of it.

They also crushed the dryer vent when they put it back into the laundry room, my husband had to pull the dryer out and put it back to the condition it was in before they took it out.

The green plastic on the floor from the front door to the basement door that roto rooter used to walk in and out of my house was never disposed of. 

They never "cleaned" the appliances like they documented we have pictures to provide proof of all....

The technicians did not listen to what our concerns were, such as covering all of our belongings, they said they would, "take care of it".

Brian and Robert did not cover our belongings, which inturn left a residue of poop particles, dry wall, mold and chemicals used during and throughout the mitigation. I have dell computer monitors that have a thick residue, my desk with everything on it, my couch, my records, my dresser drawers.  It's sad that they only covered the top of my queen bed and left everything exposed. Including the headboard to my queen bed, which is now trash thanks to Roto Rooter.

The door to the affected bedroom was somehow closed after they started the dryer treatment, which we did not find out until 2 days later. We were told to not go downstairs because of the debris in the air.

reviews.author: Heather G.
reviews.text:
I called on a Sunday evening for a plumbing call to fix my hot water heater.

We scheduled the service call for the following day, Monday, 7-11pm (after I get home from work). 

Monday at 8:30pm, they called and said they don't actually have skilled enough plumbers available after 5pm so they'd have to reschedule my job for the next day.

They claimed they left me a message to tell me at 5:30pm Monday (they did not leave any messages).

1) If they don't have skilled plumbers available after 5pm weekdays, why did the person who took my original call schedule service for 7-11pm? Their outgoing phone message clearly states that they provide "after hours plumbing service" - but apparently not if you need someone skilled enough to deal with a water heater! I clearly stated in the original call that my water heater needed service. So their marketing is misleading.

2) If they couldn't perform the service 7-11pm, why didn't someone notice it when they looked at their schedule Mon AM and call me as soon as possible to reschedule or allow me to cancel? I could have had all day Monday during biz hours to find another plumber. Instead, they waited to call me at 8:30pm, probably because waiting to tell me after normal business hours would increase the odds that'd I'd reschedule the appt. with them.

3) They did NOT leave any messages earlier, as they claimed. 

I spoke to a dispatch manager about my disatisfaction with their customer service. To his credit, he listened, was not defensive, and promised that they would learn from their mistakes to avoid these situations in the future.

But that does NOT remedy the fact that I have no hot water - AGAIN for another day. Common sense, good business practices and mindful service would have saved me a huge headache in finding another plumber and paying expensive emergency fees.

reviews.author: Kelsey P.
reviews.text:
TL;DR - Mike (employee # 1051) is awesome and solved our problem for a fair price in about an hour after a LOT of prior drama. If you have a tough job that other plumbers can't figure out, call and ask for him!

We started with a different plumber that was sent by our home warranty company, and it was a mess. He did the repair he was sent to do but didn't test it, and told us the pipe needed to be snaked as well and he would be coming back to do it. Well, the previously slow-draining sink never drained again after he repaired the pipe that was broken, and the plumber went radio-silent on us for weeks.  This ended up being a typical red tape nightmare that is typical of home warranties, but that's a story for a different review. 

Eventually, we called in Roto-rooter and it turned out to be a lot more complicated than just snaking the drain. Two different techs ended up coming to the house to try and solve the problem and ultimately sent in a camera. For all three of those events, I paid only the original service fee. 

Unfortunately, the camera got hopelessly stuck in our pipes (it got caught on the fix done by the first plumber), and they had to call in a more experienced plumber to unf*ck it.  He was able to both free the camera and clear the blockage from our pipe for a fair price. 

While the whole ordeal was definitely more expensive than I was counting on, I don't feel that I was misled or price gouged at any point. And Roto-rooter didn't charge us any significant cash until they were able to fix the problem. I feel good both about Mike and about the company. And they came out on a Saturday and solved our problem by Wednesday despite the fact that it took multiple peple and multiple visits to resolve. I would defintiely use them again.

reviews.author: Stacy C.
reviews.text: I contacted roto-rooter after we had our home inspection done and was told we had some roots in our sewer line and was recommended to clean them out.  We weren't having any problems, we just wanted the roots out as we are re-doing our basement and didn't want any future problems.  The first guy (Ariel) came out to our home who was supposed to clean out the roots, (who never did) found one of the pipes was a little off set in our front yard that connects to the city line.  They had a second guy (Mike) come out to give us a quote for a spot repair of the off set pipe.  The quote was so ridiculous I wanted to laugh.  When the second plumber came out I told him Ariel never cleaned out the pipe and that there were still roots in the pipe.  He just agreed with me and said "we can't guarantee to clean roots out."  So basically we paid over $300 for them come out and tell me that there are roots in our line (which we already knew from our inspection report) and that our pipe was a little off set and that it will cost me an arm and a leg to have a pipe spot repaired in our front yard. It's pretty frustrating when you contact a company to clean out some roots and they don't do the job. Today I had another plumber come out from a different company that quoted me at 1/4 of the price roto-rooter did and they didn't charge me over $300 to tell me something I already knew.  Actually, they didn't charge me anything.  Just an FYI, all of these good reviews that are written by customers are so they can have an attempt at getting their money back.  After roto-rooter comes out to your house they offer you to write a review and be put into a drawing that will get a full refund of their money.

reviews.author: Tasha G.
reviews.text:
I had the worst experience with roto-rooter first I call and schedule a appointment for them to come out and the tech that came out to my business property didn't bring the equipment with him and their dispatch didn't even call me back with a ETA of someone else coming out. I had to call back and get a new appointment for another tech to come out with another time frame which they never showed up so I had to reschedule it again.
The second thing when the tech came out he couldn't even unclogged the toilets I had and had to get a senior tech out to help and even the senior tech had a hard time they had to bring another tech out to assist. They were supposed to come out the next day to fix my sewer leak and they never showed up so I did it myself and then when I called to unclog a sink the tech left a huge mess in my tenants business I had to go clean up.
And the Third thing was the Roto-Rooter was supposed to call to get a video scoop of my sewer lines and their dispatch never called and every time I called to schedule no video tech came out for almost two months it took them to call me back and schedule a tech to come out this past Saturday no one called to give me a ETA I had to call again and their dispatch stated that they have more tech's on Sunday then Saturday then the time frame was supposed to be between 8-9 and the tech called and I had to reschedule for the following day so I don't recommend them unless you actually talk to a tech but Good Luck because you lost my business for my property Roto Rooter.

reviews.author: Emily G.
reviews.text:
We had a clog in our main septic line... Roto-Rooter sent two young kids out. They were polite and tried to be helpful but it seems like they didn't actually know what they were doing. They said that we needed to run a camera through our line because the snake wasn't going all the way through. They insisted that our septic tank was almost full and needed to be pumped before they could even run the camera (Turns out the tank, which had just been pumped within the past year, was totally fine). The next day they sent out a supervisor, who was able to run the camera and did clear a clog. He then tried to hard sell us on $7500 to tear out our bathtub, break through a 4" concrete slab, and replace a 6" piece of older pipe that hasn't caused us any problems (we had been warned that this company commonly tries to upsell these huge, expensive, unnecessary excavation projects). Then they left our bathroom a mess... they did not re-caulk the toilet, and there was nasty brown septic liquid sprayed all over the walls and floor and smeared on the toilet. I don't expect plumbers to be housekeepers, I expect to do some sanitizing once they leave, but for what we paid for the work they did I do expect a little bit of basic cleanup and for the toilet to be recaulked. 

Two stars because they did actually come out quickly and they did clear our clog, but the rest of the experience was a stressful mess.

reviews.author: Dana F.
reviews.text:
Roto Rooter cause extra damages to my house above the normal damages of repairing my sewage pipe.. I called several to discuss the matter. Took and sent it to them. They said they would look into it and get back with me. They never got back to me. I called several after to follow up. Agian no one ever got back to me. The damages that were done. My Laundry Pedestal looked brand new before the workers came. The next day when I got over the sticker shock for the cost of the repair, I notice a hole and crack in my Laundry Pedestal as if the Jack Hammer that they used to rip up my tile to get to the pipe hit it.  Also after they were finished draining my pipe, the machine that used spilled sewage on my whit carpet. They tried cleaning that up and I tried with my home steam cleaner but the stain is still there. 

Since they charged me $6800 to repair my pipe, you would think the company would be responsible for any other damages they caused except for the damage of tearing up my tile. 

The price of $6800 is hard for me to justified since the material they used to repair my pipe would not cost them more than a $1000 and it took 3 guys 8 hours this included transport time to complete the job.  I had a 10 ft sewage pipe replaced. I am wondering what cost $5800 to justified the total cost.

reviews.author: Cam M.
reviews.text: I called an Evergreen number for service but Evergreen does not show up on Roto-Rooter list.  Decided to post here simply because I am not going to just drop it.  BBB is next. The laundry room floor drain was clogged so I gave them a call as I've used them before for around $100.  They eventually showed up 26 hours late.  When I called the 2nd day after they missed another appointment, I was told they were busy and would be here whenever they could get here.  Finally showed up - finished 20 min. later.  The 20 min. included chatting at front door, looking at drain while I flushed toilet, going back out to vehicle for machine to use on clog.  Actual "work" took about 3 min. and then I was ripped off for $389 - and no - that is not a typo. So if you need a drain cleaned out, call the outfit on Yelp charging $35 right now or any of the places that charge around $100 bucks for something so simple.  Just don't call Roto-Rooter unless you have lots of time and money to waste.

reviews.author: Miriah B.
reviews.text: We called in this morning for an emergency call when we noticed our basement toilet, shower and laundry drain had all backed up.  They told me they would have someone out in the morning.  They hadn't called or shown up by 11:00am so I called dispatch again and said someone would call me back, at 12:00pm no one had still called so I called again.  Finally got someone that said they would have their next available truck to our house.  They finally came around 1:00pm.  The technicians that came to the house turned my poor view with the dispatch into a positive view.  They were professional, knowledgeable and very helpful.  They were able to fix the blockage and give us a solution of why we got backed up.  I would recommend the technicians to everyone.  I am glad I didn't call anyone else when I was frustrated with the dispatch office.  They do good, honest work for a reasonable price!

synthesis.summary: Same chain as the Dallas Roto-Rooter, same pattern in Lakewood: refusal to quote over the phone, prices 3-5x competitors ($389 to snake a floor drain that cost $79 down the street), and water-mitigation work that escalates from $5,500 to $8,200 with 'flaws and inconsistency.' Dakota and Christopher show up in honest 5-star reviews — but they're outliers in a sea of pricing complaints.
strengths: Dakota cleared a main-line sewer backup and returned days later to fix a small clean-out leak
Christopher worked a backed-up main floor drain into the evening, opened it by 7:30pm
weaknesses: $606 'flat rate' plus $214 labor for a 1-hour garbage disposal swap in a condo
$405 quoted to root a main line; the customer regularly pays $100 for the same service
Refuses to quote drain snaking over the phone — multiple reviewers say it's leverage to charge whatever they want once on site
redFlags: Tech reportedly told a customer to 'go fuck myself' when she questioned a $500 charge for a clogged drain
Water mitigation work escalated from $5,500 quote to $8,200 actual, with belongings left uncovered and damaged
Multiple no-shows where techs show up 5+ hours late with zero communication, sometimes near 11pm
synthesis.emergencyNotes: Some genuine same-day and Saturday-night emergency dispatches reported, but offset by 5-hour late arrivals, no-call no-shows, and dispatcher errors that send techs the wrong day.
synthesis.platformDiscrepancy: Yelp 2.8★ vs Google 4.8★ across 40 Yelp reviews — a 2.0★ gap that points to heavy review filtering on the Google rating

reviews.author: Jai's Tasteaments (Jai)
reviews.text:

I feel like a better job of communicating could be done between them and the city when it comes to time frames of arrivals for inspections but Bubba explained that also. reviews.author: Mark Kessler
reviews.text: Douglass Wolf came to our home on icy roads to help us with our hot water heater. He did a great job and let us know exactly what was going on with our heater. Very knowledgeable. Thankful for his expertise and workmanship.

reviews.author: C B.
reviews.text: Their driver cut us off, and numerous others, on highway 183 doing about 20 miles over the speed limit with no signal. Wouldn't use them for anything. I'd leave 0 stars if I could.

reviews.author: Annette C.
reviews.text: They will overcharge you based on your zip code/house size. I used All Masters twice. The first time I obtained a clear quote over the phone. A gentleman came out and fixed the issue - he tried to charge about $100 more than what I had agreed to, but once I explained, he honored the price with minimal fuss. Good enough experience where I called them back for a (separate) second issue that happened a few months later. They would not provide a quote over the phone. When they came, they indicated a bathroom faucet needed replacing and quoted me over $900. Before I could push them out the door they lowered it to $750 if I would sign that day. I ordered the faucet for $250 from Home Depot, waited 10 days for it to arrive, then replaced it in 30 minutes with minimal plumbing experience. I feel they saw my nicer home and tried to take advantage of me. I would avoid this company and use another. Also interesting is that their website shows "409 Yelp reviews" of 4+ stars, but I could only find this one where I am posting this review, which has 9, mostly bad reviews. Be careful with using this company....

reviews.author: Leigh S.
reviews.text:
I hired ALL MASTERS and they wanted $2150.00 to repair a leak in our yard. My husband had already dug a hole and found a leaking pipe blue pipe.  They wanted half upfront which I paid and Wade Benson told my husband and I that the remaining balance would be collected once the work was completed. They came out the next day and dug a bigger area in the yard and left. Wade Benson Technician came back and  wanted Thousands of dollars to repair the water line. He stated that it was 100 feet and that they charge $100 a foot and came up with price of $10,000. He attempted to collect half of the $5000 and and include the rest of the original amount in the final cost. I got him to take out the remaining balance on first repair which didn't happen but I paid $1,075 for them to dig a hole.
They got a crew out the next day to begin the line repair and I got a call from my husband stating that they were requesting the remaining balance of $5,000 and then they would have the work inspected and then fill in the now 3 holes including torn up shrubs, grass and plants in my front yard. Luckily they didn't have to dig a trench because they were able to do it underground. I was told that they cannot always do the underground method but that if a trench was required, it would not cost me any more from us. I told my husband that I would not be paying the final payment until the work is done and inspected by the city inspector. I asked about a permit but my husband stated that they had not provided a copy of the permit.
I called their office and talked to a gal at the office and she had told my husband that the work had already been inspected. She told me that she made a mistake and it had not been inspected ( same thing I read in another guys review, problem is, I didn't see that review until it was too late). I told the lady that I would not be paying until the work was completed. After a heated discussion and her telling me what I am going to do. At this time, the CITY inspector is to come tomorrow and according to the lady in office, the crew to fill the holes cannot come until Friday. I told the lady I had no problem with them coming Friday and that I had no problem paying them but that I had read bad reviews regarding them not finishing the job by leaving the holes open.

At this time I am still happy to complete the transaction if the CITY inspector is on the up and up and this company is on the up and up as well. I checked the Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners and could not find this company nor Responsible Master Plumber Bryan Barnes M-39664 and he is not listed as licensed.

reviews.author: Sonya F.
reviews.text: I wish I could leave a zero star review! These people are scammers. I don't know how they have any good ratings. Probably because they wrote them all themselves. I had a leak that I noticed because of the stain on the roof of my garage and I called All Masters Plumbing on 4/16/19 to send someone to check it out. They sent a technician who looked for a long time and seemed like he couldn't find the problem. He cut out a square in the roof of my garage to look at the plumbing which costed me $150. Then he asked us to pour water on the gasket of my upstairs bathtub to see if the leak was coming from there. He said he saw the leak and that's where it's coming from. He said the whole gasket needed to be replaced which would cost $275. The total came out to $425 and we were told we would have to pay half and he will come back the next day to change out the gasket because he didn't have the part on him. We paid $212.50 but the whole thing felt fishy because he seemed like an inexperienced technician and did not seem to know what he was doing. The next morning I climbed up and looked into the hole he cut out and asked my mother to pour water on the gasket like he told us to do the previous night to see if I noticed any leak. There was not any signs of leaking or water dripping. So, we called another company for a second opinion. They sent a technician who told us all we needed was to get some grout sealer from home depot to patch the cracks near the bath tub. This company didn't even charge us for coming out. I called All Masters Plumbing on 4/17 for a refund which the said would be $62.50 (the lady that answered the phone was not apologetic and was nonchalant about the whole situation) since we wouldn't be refunded for the $150 because he cut a hole in the roof of my garage which I expected but after a whole month still did not receive any checks from them. I almost forgot about the refund too, bet they we counting on it. Called them again on 5/23 regarding the refund that still was not received. (The lady on the phone said they forgot to send it out! Yeah, sure I bet they never planned on sending it out anyways). Called again on 5/27 because still no refund was recieved and was told because Monday was a holiday, it was delayed. Finally, recieved the refund yesterday. This company is just trying to scam customers of their money and providing half assed services. Very unprofessional please do not use this company and get scammed like I did.

reviews.author: Brent C.
reviews.text:
Brent C.

This company only wants to replace where there is a problem. They don't want to fix anything, and they overcharge. 

All-Masters Plumbing takes advantage of the consumer. 

The only good reviews they have are on Google, and they can manipulate the Google reviews. Before using this company, please check Yelp, Facebook, or any other review service.

When you call the office, you can't get an answer. They are very good at getting you off the phone without giving you any information. They always say I'll have someone call back, but they never do. 

I rate them a negative 10. Don't sign their contract. They will make you pay for everything before they start work if you call them about it. They only say it is in your contract. They won't break out the work on your invoice which causes problems with the claims adjusters and makes it almost impossible to figure out what you are paying for. They will only give you a total. 

We had stopped up waste lines. They told us the Galvanized waste lines were broken and needed to be fixed. They put an insert in the line, and the insert sticks to the outer current pipe. I tell you this because I was reading the invoice, and it says if I call the city for an inspection of the insert, I will be responsible for paying to replace the original pipe. What? 
They also said they would fix the line to the front bathroom, but they didn't.  

After they fixed the waste line, they said we needed a new water heater for $4,995.00 because the 5-year-old one we had was old and had sediment in the bottom. We got a second opinion, and the second plumber fixed it for $200.00. 

Guess what happened about 4-5 days after everything had been supposedly fixed. THE WASTE LINES STOPPED UP! They had to blow the lines out again.

I got a loan to pay for the above work, and I was looking at the invoice sent to my loan company for payment to All-Masters. Guess what? They charged me $4,995.00 to the loan company, and the loan company paid All-Masters for the water heater that was never installed. If I had not noticed it in the invoice, it would have never been discovered, and All-Masters would have overbilled me by $4,995.00.

reviews.author: Gregory M.
reviews.text:
Unfortunately, I have had a lengthy interaction with this plumber. Approximately 14 months ago I was having a problem with a secondary water heater. I requested an evaluation and their recommendation was to replace the water heater. The original water heater was approximately five years old, but out of the manufacturers warranty. I question whether the water heater genuinely needed to be replaced. I think it is very possible The original water heater could have been repaired, however, I cannot confirm that at this point.

The water heater gets very limited use. Within a year from the installation, it was not working again. I attempted to schedule, and their manager was very unprofessional over the phone. Our scheduled windows were frequently missed without apology, or provisions to narrow that window or prioritize at the next schedule. They eventually replaced the heating element. This was likely the only necessary repair for the first water heater in my estimation. One month after the heating element was installed, the water heater was not producing hot water again. All master plumbers evaluated the unit and offered a $10,000 repair with an anode installed to address hard water. There was no recommendation for this to be installed at the time of the replacement. They stated it was absolutely necessary to prevent the heating element from failing repetitively. 

I had another, much more reputable plumber, evaluate the water heater.  The second opinion repair quote was less than $3000 as opposed to all masters $10,000.

It was all around a very bad experience. They scheduled and then did not show up. We wasted 4 hours of our day waiting on the tech to never arrive. This occurred multiple times with rescheduling. They made no attempt to reconcile for missed appointments. The manager was combative and rude over the phone. The owner did not return multiple request for phone calls. 
In short, I would not recommend wasting your time with this plumber for even simple tasks. If your experience is anything like mine, you will waste time, money, energy, and frustration.

reviews.author: Katie H.
reviews.text: I could not recommend this company less. I will filing complaints with both the Plumbers Association and the BBB after my experience with All Masters. You would think with charging $40 a foot on average, the work would be top tier, as would the customer service. It has been the opposite. It began with a kitchen re-route, and turned into 30k worth of our lines being lined with the fancy new liner. Not only did I have to explain was was expected to be done anytime a service member showed up, but we also almost never saw the same face twice. Maybe high turn around. Once out re-route was complete, they begin to do the liner and it was downhill from there. Our home flooded 4 total times while the work was being performed. When they "finished" the project and had it "inspected", they called for the final payment so they could bury our lines finally, after 2 weeks worth of delays and constantly being unable to use our plumbing. We noticed the spot under the city line was leaking, and the liner was bent. So I was curious how it passed inspection. After calling around, I discovered that the inspection was never performed because they never got the permits to do the work. At this point, I had lost all trust in this company. They charge for a permit, and they planned to pocket the money and bury the problem in the line. I demanded they fix the liner, obtain permits, have it inspected, and bury my lines because I was ready to hand over my final payment. After much back and forth and heated arguments with the office and josh and Dan, we agreed to a cashiers check once the diggers were on site. The company told me repeatedly they have no reason to believe I would give them the money, even though I had paid 2/3 of the job at this point. They then attempted to leave without my burying my lines once they had the check in hand before I ended up having to threaten to file complaints formally. This has been one of the worst business experiences in my life. DO NOT USE ALL MASTERS. THEY WILL LIE AND POCKET YOUR MONEY, all while boasting a ten year warranty that you'll never use.

reviews.author: Ruth J.
reviews.text: My warranty company paid for the initial drain stoppage in my yard. Had to call them back because the problem continued. This time, they ran the camera and discovered that I had a broken line as well as a lot of tree roots in the line. They then came back to replace the pipes. After inspections, they came back to cover up the hole. Everything as far as I knew was fine until it started to rain a few days later. I quickly found out that they did not pack the dirt under my sidewalk which created a stream type path under the sidewalk in my yard and extended to the city sidewalk. I called them and let them know that this was happening. I was told by Haley (not sure about the spelling) that they would come out and take care of this.  It rained off and on for a week so once it stopped, I called back to ask about it again. Was told that it would get done. No time or date given. A week later called back again. Told me that I could talk to the owner who never came to the phone, but would call me back. No callback. A week later, the same. After this, I got the warranty company involved. I stayed on the line while they talked to them. Promised that they would come out that day. No show. Repeat with the warranty company again the next day. Same result.  These people will get the money and LIE, LIE, LIE. I know that my warranty company paid them $3200 just for the line replacement, not to mention the other calls. I was tired of looking at my yard with this compromised sidewalk, so I did it myself. I didn't need it to fall in. I am a senior citizen who cannot afford to pay for these extras. It took me 3 hours because I had to level out some other parts. I have back problems from a rear-end collision that I know will flare up from shoveling. Thank you, All Masters for not being truthful.  You may have done me wrong today, but karma has a way of making it all work out. Seen it too many times.

reviews.author: Kathy M.
reviews.text:
All Masters repiped my entire home.  The service started out UNPROFESSIONAL because one of the employees had a serious potty mouth and had no couth in my opinion.  The work started out being done in a timely manner; however,once they were paid, they started dragging their feet to complete the job when they were told well in advance that I had an upcoming trip out of the state. They assured me that they could be done before my trip.  I found myself constantly calling as to when the job would be completed only to listen to various staff members, mostly females, who were well-trained in apologizing, cautious with their excuses, and basically lying for their employees' no-show behaviors.  I had to conduct business with them while I was visiting my family in another whole state!  It was a frustrating experience and the city of Desoto red-flagged the plumbing job at the end because their so-call professionals neglected to do what they knew the city required for plumbing inspections (adding of insulation). They didn't have a choice but to correct their flaws. Secondly, one of the workers didn't turn off my pipes while they were in the process of doing the job.  Water ended up in my living room floor as well as the kitchen and nook. The head employee (Potty-Mouth) of the job informed the company, but I didn't get so much as an apology from the company...totally unprofessional!  
   Finally, the machinery used by one of their employees to get to my outdoor water line tore up an area of my neighbor's yard! They did repair his yard after my repeated calls and persistence about the issue.  I would never use this company again! Their easy offer of financing is attractive, but it is my belief that they over-price customers, and have little to no professional ethics.  They need to change their name because the only thing they are masters in is DECEIT!!!!!

reviews.author: Jo V.
reviews.text: HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE!!!!! Full of FALSE PROMISES and LIES!!! My elderly mother needed someone to come out to fix a broken spigot that was pumping out gallons of water into her yard and threatened to flood her house. The city water department came out and was unable to turn it off from the street so she called All Masters that is advertised as 24/7 (the first lie) and scheduled for someone to come at between 2am - 6 am. NO ONE CAME. She called them back at 6:34 am and they said "we don't know why no one came out. We will call a supervisor and they will call you right back." 45 minutes later, NO CALL. So my mom called again and she received a text at 7:43 am with Alberto Sanchez en route to her home. She then receives another text at 7:54 am that another plumber, Junior Aviles, was he was en route to her home. One hour later, NO ONE SHOWED UP!!! At almost 9am, someone from the city water department said they would come out to try to fix it for her so she called All Masters back to say forget it since it was clear no one was going to show up in any kind of timely manner, to which the representative said "okay" and hung up. They sure took their sweet time getting someone out to her house after no one showed up in the initial time frame they promised, but they were quick to collect her credit card information for the service call fee!!!! WILL NEVER USE THEM OR RECOMMEND THEM TO ANYONE!!!! Don't advertise 24/7 emergency plumbing if it's BS because that's called FALSE ADVERTISING.

reviews.author: Will C.
reviews.text:
We felt completely taken advantage of after working with All Masters Plumbing and I would highly recommend not using this company. The price they charged us for the work was near criminal. Plus, I have heard that most of their reviews are paid for and fake so be weary. I would leave a 0 star review if possible.

The technicians seem to be trained to scare the customer into paying for things they don't need then over charging for the job.

For example they quoted us on a job they said was "necessary" to replace our water heater for a price of $5k while another plumber came out and fixed the issue for $200. This other plumber even mentioned they have heard numerous horror stories about All Masters Plumbing taking advantage of people.

In another situation, we had an emergency and we decided to go with All Masters Plumbing because they said they could get out there and fix it right away. Turns out they Over Promised, Under Delivered, and Over Charged. I'm genuinely embarrassed to admit the amount they charged us for the work they did. It makes me sick to my stomach and the only reason we went with them is because we were in an emergency situation. Then, once they started the job the cost of the project kept going up and up. Again, we felt completely taken advantage of.

In addition, their customer service was terrible, I would consistently call in and ask for updates, they would tell me they would call me back and never did.

I would highly recommend not working with this company.

reviews.author: Nancy L.
reviews.text: All Masters Plumbing (AMP) was the assigned plumber through Service Line Warranties to determine a leak in our front yard. It was the irrigation line and not the city line. The leak became a gusher once the earth was removed and I hired AMP to repair the leak. While repairing the leak, the plumber determined our pressure was dangerously high and would (over time) damage large appliances on the line. We researched it and agreed, so hired AMP to install a pressure regulator. Big mistake. Could not take a shower and run faucet at the same time. Pressure ridiculously low. Since the regulator was installed, AMP came out 2 more times to open the valve, had me sign a statement that I requested to increase the pressure. Was told that we should spend another 2K+ to change the water line to a quarter inch larger. Husband also opened the valve to max. Still pressure problems. I called AMP to remove the pressure regulator 3 of 4 times, even threaten to leave this bad review. No response except for the receptionist said she would pass the message to the supervisor. I am NOT a plumber and mistakenly relied upon AMP to know how the regulator would affect the water pressure. After spending over $800 with AMP on the regulator, I now have to spend $650+ with another plumber to have it removed. And just learned that AMP used a 'shark bite' that is prone to leaking.  You have been warned...do not use this plumber.

synthesis.summary: All Masters Plumbing has a Google 4.5 against a Yelp 2.5 across 91 reviews — and the Yelp reviews tell a brutal story: $7,500 for a single toilet swap, $850 to blow out an AC condensation line, missed appointments, and refunds that take 2 years to fight for. BBB A+ doesn't match the Yelp pattern.
strengths: Initial sales response is fast — they will get someone on your calendar quickly
weaknesses: Pricing is the dominant complaint — '$7,500 and four weeks to get a new toilet', '$450 to change two hose bibs', '$5k gas water heater quote vs $1,300 elsewhere'
Repeated allegations of taking advantage of elderly customers
Multiple reports of arriving outside the scheduled window — 'team arrived 3 separate times outside the scheduled window'
Initial sales quote and final invoice differing by tens of thousands — 'differed by over $20,000'
redFlags: Allegation of charging in advance and never completing work — '2 years now on a refund for work paid for and not completed'
Pattern of missed appointments and rescheduling without notice
Reviewers describe high-pressure sales targeting elderly customers
One review alleges flooding caused by their work, with no follow-up
Yelp 2.5 vs Google 4.5 across 91 Yelp reviews — major divergence suggesting review curation
synthesis.emergencyNotes: Multiple reviewers describe paying for after-hours emergency dispatch and getting no-show or 1-3am appointment windows that were silently abandoned. Stated emergency capacity does not appear reliable.
synthesis.platformDiscrepancy: Yelp 2.5 vs Google 4.5 across 91 Yelp reviews — extreme divergence suggesting review curation or fake reviews
